Title: NUBE-MCBA dispute: Ramanan's appeal to continue for court ruling on legal issues, says ministry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The continuation of Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan's appeal in the dispute between the National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) and the Malaysian Commercial Banks' Association (MCBA) is aimed at obtaining a Court of Appeal ruling on legal issues arising from the High Court's decision, the ministry said today.
In a statement, the Human Resources Ministry said the continuation of the appeal did not mean the ministry was closing the door to an amicable settlement through negotiations between the two parties.
"The human resources minister did not apply for a stay of execution of the High Court's decision, while the Department of Industrial Relations Malaysia had taken proactive steps by summoning the parties involved to resume conciliation proceedings.
"However, MCBA exercised its right to apply for a stay of execution of the High Court's decision, and the application was granted by the Court," the ministry said.
The statement added that the stay order had prevented negotiations on the collective agreement from proceeding for as long as the order remained in force.
In this regard, the ministry clarified that Ramanan's withdrawal of the appeal would not automatically allow negotiations between NUBE and MCBA to resume, as the stay order obtained by MCBA remained in force.
The media had previously reported that the dispute between MCBA and NUBE involved the payment of festive assistance and the 20th Collective Agreement.
On Feb 13, the High Court allowed NUBE's application for judicial review, quashed two references made by the human resources minister to the Industrial Court and directed both parties to resume negotiations.
However, on Sept 26, the High Court allowed MCBA's application to stay the execution of the decision pending the association's appeal at the Court of Appeal.  — BERNAMA

Title: Musk's futuristic Cybertruck rolls towards exit
Article:
WASHINGTON: Production of Cybertrucks — the pickups hailed by enthusiasts as a symbol of Elon Musk's futuristic ambitions and equally hated as ugly reminders of the Donald Trump era — will wind down, the Tesla chief executive said on Friday.
Tesla will stop building the truck at its Texas factory around the middle of 2027 to free up space for its Cybercab robotaxi, Musk said.
"Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote on X.
Musk did not say whether the truck would be built elsewhere or discontinued altogether, nor what would happen to outstanding orders.
Wes Morrill, the Cybertruck's lead engineer, wrote in a separate post that the truck "was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab".
"Thanks to everyone who contributed to making the future (look) like the future," he added.
Tesla fans lamented the departure of the Cybertruck on X, the social media platform Musk owns, but the tycoon reassured them that the Cybertruck fleet "will be around for a long time".
The truck came to be seen as an extension of Musk himself, and its image became entangled with his politics as he took on a high-profile role leading the Trump administration's cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency. Some owners reported vandalism and harassment.
The angular stainless-steel behemoth was unveiled in November 2019, and Musk said at the time that it had drawn 250,000 pre-orders within days.
Production was originally slated for 2021 but was repeatedly delayed, with customer deliveries starting in late 2023.
Tesla built its Texas production lines with planned capacity of 250,000 trucks a year, but sales have come nowhere near that figure.
As US demand slumped, Tesla began selling the truck abroad, starting deliveries in South Korea in November 2025 and in the United Arab Emirates in January.
Tesla does not break out Cybertruck revenue, but its "other models" category, which includes the pickup, accounts for just a small percentage of sales.
Cox Automotive estimated total sales of just 72,702, with more than half in 2024 and sales fading thereafter.
The truck has also been subject to multiple recalls and complaints over build quality.
The Cybercab, a two-seat vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals, was unveiled in October 2024.
Tesla began production at the Texas plant in April and started offering paid Cybercab rides in Austin in September through its existing Robotaxi service.
"The decision to discontinue the Cybertruck highlights how difficult it can be to translate strong initial attention and enthusiasm around a new vehicle into sustainable mainstream demand," said Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive.
Tesla saw the vehicle as a bid for the giant US pickup truck market, but it quickly became a "niche" product, Valdez Streaty said.
The robotaxi is central to Musk's effort to recast Tesla as an artificial intelligence and robotics company rather than a carmaker, though its success depends on the company delivering fully driverless technology, which it has yet to demonstrate at scale.

Title: Dozens of pilot whales stranded on New Zealand coast
Article:
SYDNEY: Dozens of pilot whales have been found stranded on a beach on New Zealand's North Island, and rescuers are trying to refloat a handful of survivors, the country's conservation department said on Thursday.
At least 20 pilot whales were stranded along the Ngawi coast near Cape Palliser, the southernmost point of the North Island, the Department of Conservation said.
The department said it was working with local iwi — a Maori tribe — and Project Jonah, a group that specialises in rescuing stranded whales. Two whales had been successfully refloated so far.
Locals said up to 50 whales had been stranded along the coastline overnight, Radio New Zealand reported.
Most had succumbed to their injuries, and volunteers were trying to keep the survivors alive and hydrated using buckets of water and towels.
[[nid:1572635]]
"It's horrible. The ones that are alive are on their last breaths," Ngawi local Rob Bargh told Radio New Zealand.
In a Facebook post on Thursday, Project Jonah said four whales were alive and rescuers would try to refloat them during high tide.
Whale strandings are fairly common in New Zealand and neighbouring Australia because of the large populations of pilot whales living in the deep oceans surrounding both island nations. The cause of whale strandings is unknown.

Title: Make halal certification compulsory for slaughterhouses, govt told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Slaughterhouse operators should be required to obtain Malaysian Halal Certification to address confusion among Muslims over the halal status of food products.
A source said the move had become increasingly urgent following a series of media exposés raising concerns about food consumed by Muslims.
The source said making halal certification mandatory was the only way to protect Muslims from the risk of consuming poultry that had not been slaughtered in accordance with Islamic requirements, as highlighted in a recent incident.
Some slaughterhouses, the source claimed, continued to disregard not only hygiene standards but, more worryingly, Islamic slaughtering requirements.
The source said a proposal to make halal certification compulsory for all slaughterhouse operators, restaurant owners and food manufacturers was brought before the cabinet in 2024.
However, the proposal was not implemented after it met with opposition from cabinet members.
Among the concerns raised was that mandatory halal certification could negatively affect non-Muslim business operators, who might perceive the requirement as forcing them to apply for certification.
"The cabinet did not agree at the time because of concerns over negative reactions from those opposing the policy.
"That is why we have retained the same policy to this day. Even after 52 years since Malaysia introduced halal certification, we have chosen to take a step backwards," the source said.
He said the voluntary nature of halal certification had created confusion, particularly among Muslims, over whether food producers complied with halal requirements.
A check by BH of a written parliamentary record dated Oct 14, 2024, showed that the government had decided to retain its existing voluntary halal certification policy.
The policy is administered by the Islamic Development Department, state Islamic religious departments and state Islamic religious councils.
The voluntary halal certification policy has remained unchanged since its introduction in 1974.

Title: "I am still the menteri besar,' says Ismail amid replacement speculation
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declined to comment on speculation that he would be replaced by Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias.
Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, said that he remained the menteri besar and that there was no question of him stepping down from the post.
"As of today, I am still the menteri besar," he said briefly after attending the Little India Deepavali Bazaar Carnival last night.
He was responding to questions about claims linking Jalaluddin, who is Pertang assemblyman, to the state's top post.
Ismail also declined to comment on the opposition's claim that the state legislative assembly sitting scheduled for Nov 26 might be postponed.
"Let's not get into that. This time, let's celebrate Deepavali first," he said, urging all parties to focus on the Deepavali celebrations.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the state government had allocated RM70,000 for the Little India Deepavali Bazaar Carnival, which included contributions to the Indian community in rural areas.
He said the state government planned to discuss gazetting the Little India area to attract tourists.
"This matter will be discussed in detail with the Seremban City Council mayor, as the proposed area extends about 100m to 400m beyond the original site and has the potential to become a tourist attraction," he said.
He said about 7,000 visitors were expected to attend the Negri Sembilan-level Deepavali open house at the Seremban City Council hall on Nov 14, from 11am to 4pm.
He said a variety of dishes representing the state's diverse communities and cultures, particularly traditional Indian food, would be served to allow visitors to enjoy a range of delicacies in a spirit of goodwill.
"The state government invites all Negri Sembilan residents to attend the Deepavali celebrations in large numbers to foster goodwill among the community.
"Our aim is to ensure that every celebration is held in a lively, harmonious and joyful atmosphere, strengthening ties among communities and reinforcing the unity that already exists," he said.
In a separate development, he said a proposal to gazette the Dato Lee Fong Yee area as Seremban's Little India would be discussed in detail with the Seremban City Council mayor.

Title: Puncak Alam's rapid development brings flooding, traffic woes
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: Rapid growth in Bandar Puncak Alam, also known as Bandar Shah Alam 2, has outpaced infrastructure development, leaving its nearly 250,000 residents grappling with mounting problems.
Spanning more than 6,000ha, the township, once dubbed Waterfall City, is now home to at least six major property developments.
However, essential infrastructure has yet to be upgraded, raising concerns among residents.
Development encroaching on hilly areas is also putting pressure on the environment, raising concerns over slope stability and environmental sustainability.
Among the main problems are flash floods, with drainage systems allegedly unable to cope with rapid development, and severe traffic congestion caused by a road network that has failed to keep pace with the growing number of vehicles.
Poorly planned development has also been linked to an increased risk of road accidents, while several essential facilities remain incomplete despite years of residential expansion.
Puncak Alam Residents' chairman Mohd Hanif Md Sultan said residents were concerned that infrastructure development had fallen behind despite the township's rapid growth and numerous high-impact projects.
"I understand that Puncak Alam contributes substantial tax revenue, not only from residents but also from companies setting up factories and offices here. Yet, the facilities remain inadequate and have not kept pace with development.
"We still do not have a police station or a fire station, despite the rapid population growth. Severe traffic congestion caused by roads that cannot accommodate the number of vehicles is also putting immense pressure on residents.
"The drainage system is also problematic despite maintenance work. Flash floods can happen at any time, and there is even the possibility of a major flood disaster.
"The authorities should also look into the recent case of a child who fell into a drain and whose body was eventually found," he told BH.
He said residents had raised their concerns, including through letters to the local authority, but had yet to see satisfactory solutions.
Hanif, who is mulling action, including bringing the matter to the attention of the authorities and the Selangor palace, said measures taken so far had failed to address the problems comprehensively.
He said the poorly planned road network made travelling difficult, as some access roads between residential neighbourhoods remained closed despite having been built.
This forced motorists to use main roads even when travelling between nearby housing areas.
Jeram assemblyman Harrison Hassan acknowledged that infrastructure in Puncak Alam had failed to keep pace with development and population growth, requiring urgent action by both the federal and state governments.
"Our office receives various complaints every day. Infrastructure is the main issue, including damaged and potholed roads, faulty streetlights and inconsistent domestic waste collection schedules," he said.
He said critical public facilities, including police stations, fire stations and government health clinics, fell under federal jurisdiction.
Harrison called for stronger commitment from federal agencies to bring these issues to the attention of the relevant ministries.
Former Jeram assemblyman Mohd Shaid Rosli also claimed that Puncak Alam appeared to have been neglected despite extensive development, citing delays in the construction of a school in Alam Suria.
Shaid also highlighted the shortage of essential public facilities, including a government health clinic currently operating from a terraced house.
He said this underscored the urgent need for infrastructure improvements to match the township's rapid growth.

Title: Shaharul is new Pahang police chief, 18 others transferred
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman Special Branch II deputy director Datuk Mohammad Shaharul Md Osman has been appointed the new Pahang police chief, effective Dec 7.
Police secretary Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Mashdik Yahya said the transfers involving 19 senior police officers also included the appointment of new Sabah and Sarawak police commissioners.
"Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos has been appointed Sabah police commissioner with the acting rank of commissioner of police.
"Sarawak Deputy Police Commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak has been appointed Sarawak police commissioner with the acting rank of commissioner of police," he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Pahang Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Yusri Othman has been appointed Penang deputy police chief with the acting rank of deputy commissioner.
"Sabah Internal Security and Public Order Department chief Datuk Abdul Fuad Abdul Malek has been appointed Esscom commander with the acting rank of deputy commissioner.
[[nid:1572618]]
"Penang Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zailanni Amit has been appointed Sarawak deputy police commissioner with the acting rank of deputy commissioner," he said.
Other transfers include Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, who has been appointed Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department's general policing assistant director with the acting rank of senior assistant commissioner.
"His position in Kuala Lumpur will be filled by the department's deputy chief, Superintendent Suffian Abdullah, who will assume the acting rank of assistant commissioner.
"National Financial Crime Prevention Centre integrated operations director Assistant Commissioner Yusri Mahmud has been appointed commander of the 69 Commando unit under the Special Operations Force in Ulu Kinta, Perak, with the acting rank of senior assistant commissioner," he said.
Also involved in the transfers are Johor Baru Utara district deputy police chief Superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor, who has been appointed its district police chief, and Superintendent Yampil Anak Garai, who has been appointed Lahad Datu police chief.
Both will assume the acting rank of assistant commissioner.
The transfers also involve several other senior positions in Bukit Aman, Sarawak, Sabah, Kedah and Selangor.

Title: ITU: Malaysia to propose expanding internet coverage to areas with economic activities
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia intends to propose at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) level that Internet coverage measurements should no longer focus solely on the Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) standard, but should also take into account areas where economic activities take place.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposal was being studied following complaints from the public and members of parliament about internet connectivity problems in locations without residential settlements but which serve as major transportation routes or economic activity centres.
He said the existing approach, which is based on coverage in populated areas, should be reconsidered by taking into account the concept of Coverage of Economic Areas to ensure that connectivity needs in economic areas were also given due attention.
"We want to propose at the ITU level whether it would be appropriate to reconsider the standard from COPA to Coverage of Economic Areas. We want to look beyond whether people live in a particular area and consider whether economic activities are being carried out there," he said in an interview ahead of the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) today.
Fahmi said areas that warranted attention included major roads, railway lines, ports, coastal areas used by fishermen, as well as tourism and recreational destinations.
He said these areas might not have permanent residents but still required good Internet access to support economic activities and the movement of people.
"Many have complained about Internet connectivity or their network coverage along major routes, roads and places that do not have residents but serve as links between two locations or host economic activities," he said.
Fahmi said recreational areas such as Taman Negara and the islands in Sabah were also among the locations that warranted consideration in Internet coverage planning, as they supported economic activities despite not necessarily being residential areas.
He said the proposal had the potential to broaden the approach to assessing digital connectivity needs, particularly in areas that played an important role in economic activities.
"We see a lot of need to take forward ideas such as this, which have not been discussed so far. So, Malaysia could perhaps be among the first to bring this matter to the ITU level," he said.
Fahmi is in Doha from Nov 6 to 11 to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26, with the mission of retaining the country's seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
Malaysia's participation in the ITU's highest-level conference, held every four years, also aims to ensure that the country's voice and interests continue to be represented in discussions on the global direction of telecommunications and information and communications technology development.
The move reflects the country's aspiration to remain actively involved in international strategic discussions, not merely keeping abreast of global technological developments but also contributing to shaping their direction.
Malaysia's position on the council also provides an opportunity for the country to share its experience and approaches in addressing connectivity challenges, particularly in telecommunications infrastructure development.
Apart from strengthening diplomatic ties, the membership would also enhance Malaysia's international visibility and reinforce its role in digital cooperation, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.
The ITU is a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for ICT matters, including standardisation, radio spectrum allocation and coordination of global telephone and satellite connections, as well as efforts to bridge the digital divide, worldwide.

Title: Cop injured as tree crushes motorcycle in Sungai Petani
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A policeman was injured when a falling tree crushed his motorcycle in front of a premises in Padang Temusu around midnight.
The victim, who is attached to a police station in Penang, was on his way home after completing his shift.
He sustained injuries to his head, right hand and leg.
Civil Defence Force personnel treated the man at the scene and took him to Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital.
Firefighters were deployed to the scene to cut up and remove the fallen tree.

Title: Better care support needed to keep women in the workforce
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian women have made progress in workforce participation and career advancement over the years, but experts believe a gap remains between the opportunities available to them and their ability to fully benefit from them.
They think women's empowerment should not be measured solely by their labour force participation rate but also by the quality of jobs they hold, their access to leadership positions and their ability to control their income and make independent financial decisions.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) recorded a female labour force participation rate of 56.6 per cent, compared with 83.3 percent for men, in the fourth quarter of 2025, indicating considerable room for improvement in women's economic participation.
SHARING OF RESPONSIBILITIES
Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM) Centre for Applied Psychology, Policy and Social Work senior lecturer Associate Prof Dr Rajwani Md Zain said the true measure of empowerment is the extent to which women have the choice to work, advance their careers and build financial security.
She said one of the main challenges facing women in the country is the unequal sharing of family caregiving responsibilities, particularly for single mothers and female heads of households. This is compounded by the high cost of childcare, especially in urban areas, and a lack of childcare services that align with the working hours of mothers.
Workplace cultures that lack an understanding of family needs also present a challenge – for instance, mothers who require time to breastfeed their children may not be granted any flexibility by their employers.
"These challenges vary according to income, location, employment status and the level of family support available. Therefore, (women) empowerment policies must pay particular attention to single mothers, low-income women, those in rural areas and women working in the informal sector," she said in an interview with Bernama recently.
Elaborating, Rajwani said childcare and family responsibilities significantly influence women's decisions to return to work. For instance, after childbirth, mothers have to adjust to physical recovery, breastfeeding, newborn care routines and emotional changes, while also having to meet the demands of their jobs.
Without adequate family support and access to affordable childcare, returning to work can become a daunting challenge for many mothers.
LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES
Citing DOSM's 2025 time-use data, Rajwani said women spent about six hours and seven minutes daily on unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities, including looking after babies.
This, she said, could lead women to reduce their working hours, turn down promotion opportunities or even leave their jobs altogether.
"For example, when a promotion involves relocating to another area, many women are reluctant to move away from their families.
"The consequences can be far-reaching as the loss of income also affects work experience, salary progression and retirement savings in the future.
"Women's decisions to leave their jobs should not be viewed merely as a personal choice, but examined in the context of the constraints they face and the support available to them," she said.
She said reports of child neglect and abuse at childcare institutions have heightened parents' concerns about their children's safety.
Commenting on the increase in maternity leave entitlement from 360 to 490 days for civil servants, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the 2027 Budget presentation, Rajwani described the move as recognition of mothers' recovery needs and family responsibilities.
She said the extended leave could help mothers navigate the crucial early period after childbirth more comfortably and reduce pressure to return to work earlier.
Postnatal care support could also help mothers manage their own recovery and their babies' needs, making the transition back to work easier.
"However, this measure must be complemented by support after maternity leave ends. This includes affordable, quality childcare centres with operating hours suited to working parents, particularly shift workers; breastfeeding facilities; and flexible working arrangements where job requirements permit.
"Employers should consider providing such facilities or, at the very least, offering greater flexibility to mothers, especially first-time mothers," she added.
WOMEN EMPOWERING WOMEN
Meanwhile, pointing to the care economy, which has the potential to create employment and entrepreneurship opportunities in the care services sector, Rajwani said it would enable more women to enter or return to the workforce.
She said caregiving services should not be limited to infant care but should also cover maternal care during the confinement period.
"Opportunities in prenatal and postnatal care include providing daily assistance at home, preparing meals, helping with household management and caring for mothers and babies, according to the training and competencies of service providers.
"This could also include clinical services, provided by qualified professionals," she said.
On Sept 15, Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri was reported as saying that 42.8 percent of the 4.89 million women outside the labour force cited household responsibilities and caring for family members as their main reasons for not participating in the workforce.
Commenting on the figures, Rajwani said they highlighted the link between access to caregiving support and women's economic participation, rather than indicating the number of new jobs that could be created.
She said any vacancy arising from women's withdrawal from the labour force could be filled by workers of either gender.
"Developing the care economy requires collaboration among the government, private sector and communities to provide more secure career opportunities, social protection and quality services that families can afford.
"The sector's success should not be measured solely by the well-being of those receiving care but also by whether the people providing these services receive proper recognition, protection and fair remuneration," she said.
PLATFORM SUPPORT
Among the organisations tapping into the potential of the care services sector is iBidan, a home-based prenatal and postnatal care platform.
iBidan founder Shannon Eu said her platform leverages women's traditional caregiving skills to help them earn an income without having to establish or operate their own care service centres.
It also provides mothers with opportunities to balance their career aspirations with family responsibilities.
iBidan connects experienced midwives with clients through a structured booking system, operational support, professional skills development and opportunities for midwives to build more organised careers.
The platform now has a network of more than 500 midwives in Malaysia and Singapore.
"This approach demonstrates how existing caregiving skills can be integrated into a modern service delivery system to create professional career opportunities in maternal care," Eu said.
She also said that iBidan recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Wanita Berdaya Selangor (WBS) in conjunction with the Selangor International Care Expo (SICE) 2026 that was held here recently.
WBS, a subsidiary of Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated), supports the Selangor government's women's empowerment agenda. The signing ceremony was also attended by WBS chief executive officer Siti Faridah Abdul Samad and Selangor state executive council member Anfaal Saari.
"This collaboration provides both organisations with an opportunity to explore initiatives in community education and postnatal maternal care support, as well as develop the professional skills and careers of midwives, whose jobs hold both economic and social value.
"Through this MoU, iBidan and WBS hope to explore collaborative opportunities that will support the development of a skilled female workforce and contribute to a more inclusive and sustainable care economy," Eu said.
In conjunction with SICE 2026, iBidan also organised a special forum, titled 'Building Careers. Changing Lives – Real Stories from the Women Behind iBidan', featuring three midwives who shared their experiences, challenges and career opportunities in the caregiving services sector.
The forum also explored how professional skills, easy access to clients and platform support could help women rebuild their careers while improving their families' well-being. For more information on iBidan, please visit www.ibidan.com.my or www.ibidan.com.sg. — BERNAMA

Title: Traffic congestion, several accidents reported on NSE ahead of Deepavali
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic congestion was reported along several major stretches of the North-South Expressway (NSE) from midnight, with several accidents reported ahead of tomorrow's Deepavali celebrations.
Congestion was reported on both sides of the expressway, particularly along the northbound route, while several locations experienced disruptions due to accidents and vehicle breakdowns.
According to updates by PLUS on X, traffic congestion was first reported at 12.04am along the northbound stretch from Permatang Pauh to Sungai Dua.
Similar conditions were reported from Slim River to Sungkai, Sungai Buloh Hospital to the Rawang rest and recreation (R&R) area, Jasin to Ayer Keroh, Kulai to Sedenak, and Skudai to Senai.
For southbound traffic, congestion was also reported on the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE) from Bandar Serenia to Bandar Baru Nilai.
Meanwhile, an accident at Km420.7 northbound, from Bukit Beruntung to Bukit Tagar, at 7.31am caused the emergency lane to be blocked, resulting in traffic congestion.
Several other accidents also disrupted traffic, including one at Km81 northbound, from Ayer Hitam to Yong Peng Selatan.
PLUS said the left lane was blocked following the accident, causing a 7km congestion, which had increased to 9km in an update at 3.06am.
An accident was also reported at Km354 northbound, from Slim River to Sungkai, at 3.27am, blocking the right lane and causing congestion.
However, a 4.29am update stated that the right lane had been reopened, while the emergency lane remained closed and traffic was still congested.
Other accidents were reported at Km409.6 northbound, from Lembah Beringin to Tanjung Malim, and Km315, from Tapah to Gopeng.
Meanwhile, a broken-down trailer at Km320.3 northbound, from Tapah to Gopeng, at 3.43am blocked the left lane and caused traffic congestion.
For southbound traffic, accidents were reported at Km227.3, from Pedas Linggi to Simpang Ampat; Km277.6, from Bandar Baru Nilai to Bandar Ainsdale; and Km267.2, from Bandar Ainsdale to Seremban.
A crash was also reported at Km160 southbound, from Tangkak to Bukit Gambir, blocking the emergency lane and causing congestion.
PLUS activated the SmartLane at Km151.4 to Km146.4 northbound, from Bukit Tambun Utara to Juru, to help ease traffic congestion.
According to a PLUS update at 7.41am, the SmartLane was also activated at Km159.2 to Km162.7 southbound, from Bukit Tambun Utara to Jawi.
The activation allows light vehicles to use the emergency lanes along the designated SmartLane stretches at both locations.
Meanwhile, traffic on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway and East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) was reported to be smooth in both directions as of 7am.
According to the expressway operator, congestion had earlier been reported on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway at 2.25am, involving the eastbound stretches from Genting Sempah to Bukit Tinggi and Bukit Tinggi to Lentang.
The 2km and 5.3km congestion was caused by an increase in vehicle volume, but traffic had returned to normal in updates between 2.30am and 7am.

Title: Pas: Why is Najib's house arrest still on hold? [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas has demanded an explanation from the government over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest despite the payment of his RM50 million fine.
Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan questioned why the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) was still seeking clarification on the conditional royal pardon granted nearly two months ago.
He said the pardon, announced by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department on Sept 18, clearly stipulated that
Najib could serve the remainder of his prison sentence
under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the fine.
"Under the ordinary interpretation of the law, and as understood by the public, it is clear that once the RM50 million fine has been paid, Najib should be allowed to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028," Takiyuddin said in a statement today.
He said the
A-GC's claim
that two possible interpretations of the royal pardon and the High Court's order required further examination should no longer arise.
He also questioned why the A-GC had not sought clarification earlier if its concerns were related to the High Court's rejection of an application for a stay of execution in Najib's separate 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case on Oct 14.
"If that is the issue requiring examination and consideration, the A-GC should have sought clarification from the court on that date, rather than after Najib's supporters had gone to great lengths to raise funds to settle the fine imposed on him," he said.
Takiyuddin called on the A-GC to explain why the implementation of the royal pardon appeared to have been delayed.
"The government, particularly the A-GC as the guardian of the public interest, must provide a clear explanation to the public, without hiding behind excuses, as to why the implementation of the sentence appears to have been delayed," he said.
He said the legal maxim "justice delayed is justice denied" must be upheld to ensure fairness to all parties.
Yesterday, Umno confirmed that Najib's RM50 million fine had been
paid in full
at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
However, the A-GC subsequently called for the implementation of his house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding the conditional pardon and the effect of the court orders.
The A-GC said the clarification was necessary to determine whether payment of the fine settled only the financial penalty, leaving Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest, or whether it meant the entire sentence had been completed.
The chambers maintained that the proposed deferment was not intended to challenge the King's decree but to ensure that the pardon and related court orders were implemented correctly.
Najib's lawyers
have rejected the A-GC's position and demanded his immediate transfer to house arrest.
Najib remains at Kajang Prison, where he has been serving his sentence since August 2022 following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds.
His original
12-year prison sentence
and RM210 million fine were reduced to six years and RM50 million respectively by the Pardons Board in 2024.

Title: Prince Harry seeks to appeal after losing case against UK tabloid
Article:
LONDON: Prince Harry on Friday launched a legal challenge after losing a privacy case against the publisher of the British tabloid the Daily Mail.
The case is the third and final one brought by the Duke of Sussex in his acrimonious legal battle with British tabloids.
The High Court in August ordered Harry and six others, including pop legend Elton John, to make an initial payment of £9.5 million (US$13 million) to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL) after finding against them a month earlier.
Harry, the 42-year-old younger son of King Charles III, and the other claimants were seeking to appeal on the grounds that the judgment and costs ruling were "legally and factually flawed", a statement sent to AFP by law firm Sheridans said.
The group had "today filed applications with the Court of Appeal for permission to appeal", the statement added.
The claimants in the case — who also include John's husband David Furnish and actors Elizabeth Hurley and Sadie Frost — had accused the Mail of bugging their cars and homes, listening in on calls and other privacy breaches. ANL had denied all the allegations.
The appeal bid comes after Harry, formally known as the Duke of Sussex, and his wife Meghan, 45, moved back to the UK in August with their two young children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five.
The couple left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud.
After an emotional 11-week trial — during which Harry gave in-person evidence — judge Matthew Nicklin in July sided with the newspaper publisher, concluding that the claimants had failed to prove their allegations.
After a further two-day hearing over costs, he made the initial costs decision, while again criticising the claimants' case as "speculative".
Huge costs
The court noted that ANL estimated its total costs defending itself had reached about £34.5 million by July 9.
However, the ruling noted that the High Court had not determined how much of those costs the claimants must ultimately pay.
The matter is set to be determined at a separate hearing.
Nicklin rejected requests by Harry and the others to pay

Title: Keeping the art of kolam alive, one grain at a time [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Grain by grain, Sivabalan Arumugam transforms ordinary rice grains into intricate works of art.
With nimble hands, he moves across the floor, bringing vibrant kolam designs to life.
For the 36-year-old founder of Life Creation and Design Rangoli Kolam, the temporary nature of his creations has never dampened his passion for the traditional art form.
His fascination with colour has fuelled a lifelong commitment to preserving the craft while finding new ways to bring it into modern spaces.
Sivabalan has spent nearly 21 years working professionally in the field, having started at the age of 15. His creations have adorned shopping malls and office spaces.
His dedication earned him a place in the
Malaysia Book of Records
in October 2024 for creating the "Most Colours in a Single Rangoli Kolam".
The record-setting creation measured 20 x 25 feet and featured 100 distinct shades, with Sivabalan coming up with the entire design himself.
His interest in kolam began at the age of 7, when he started creating designs at home during festive occasions such as Deepavali and Pongal.
"My father could draw very well as a mechanical engineer, and I learnt from him. I really love colours. Whenever I draw a kolam, I feel happy," he said.
Trained in graphic design, Sivabalan handles both the design and execution of his creations, relying largely on freehand techniques rather than ready-made patterns.
He draws inspiration from books, online videos and textiles, as well as frequent trips to India, where he observes locals creating kolam outside their homes and in temples.
"Every day, the people, including women and children, design kolam in front of their houses and temples.
"The kolam they draw uses only white kolam powder, which is different from the kolam we make in Malaysia," he said.
His eye for colour combinations has led him to experiment with different shades, giving each design its own character.
But bringing each design to life requires months of painstaking preparation.
Rather than relying entirely on commercially available coloured rice, Sivabalan prepares his own using broken rice and food colouring, including jelly and cake colouring.
ART THAT DOESN'T LAST
For all the hours spent preparing and arranging the rice grains, a kolam remains a temporary creation.
A large installation can take three to four months to prepare and several days to complete, only to be cleared soon after the celebrations end.
"It is sad seeing the kolam swept away after hours of hard work. But that's just how the process goes when making a kolam.
"We can only look forward to next year's celebration and come up with newer designs to make our kolam even better," Sivabalan said.
PASSING IT ON TO THE NEXT GENERATION
For Sivabalan, the fleeting nature of kolam is a reminder to value not just the finished creation, but also the skill, patience and preparation behind it.
He believes the tradition can survive only if it is passed on to those willing to learn and practise the craft, particularly younger generations.
"I definitely want to teach the younger generation so they can appreciate the culture and it won't be forgotten," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Meghan Markle's father arrested in US over child sexual abuse images
Article:
WASHINGTON: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, was arrested on Friday on a charge of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs of himself with naked underage girls, found in rented storage units in California.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry was taken into custody by federal agents in Florida, where, according to the Daily Mail, the elder Markle, who uses a wheelchair, was a nursing home patient.
"Mr. Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said in a statement.
In a criminal complaint filed on Thursday in US District Court in Los Angeles, Markle was charged with one count of "possession of child pornography".
If convicted, Markle could face up to 20 years in prison, the Justice Department said.
Markle, a resident of Lakeland, Florida, made his initial court appearance before a US magistrate judge in nearby Tampa.
The judge ordered him released pending trial on condition that he submit to home detention and electronic monitoring, the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles said in a statement.
No plea was entered, and an arraignment is not expected for several weeks, according to the statement.
Markle's defence counsel was not immediately known, and it was not clear when he might be transferred to California to face the charge against him.
According to an FBI affidavit filed as part of the criminal complaint, Markle kept the sexually explicit material in question in two Los Angeles-area storage units he had rented since 2008. Agents searched the units last week after obtaining a warrant.
Agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, 35mm film negatives and books containing child sexual abuse images, according to the affidavit.
The 13-page document stated that at least two frames on film negatives showed a man identified by a witness as Markle with a "nude pre-pubescent girl" in poses "designed to elicit a sexual response in the viewer". In one image, the man appeared to be fondling the girl's genitalia.
Buckingham Palace and a spokesperson for Meghan Markle did not respond to requests for comment.
Authorities in the Philippines, where Thomas Markle had previously lived for some time, began investigating him last month over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse images.
British police last month said they would refer allegations against him to overseas law enforcement agencies after finding that the claims had not been passed to other authorities when they were first received.
The FBI began its investigation into Markle in October, according to its affidavit, after hearing from a witness who said they had discovered suspected child abuse material among Markle's possessions in the Philippines.
The FBI also spoke last month with a second witness, who was also unidentified in the affidavit, and who said Markle rented at least one storage unit in California.
At least one of the photographs reviewed by the FBI showed that Markle was staying at a hotel or motel in the Philippines, based on the logo seen on the pillows on the bed.
Markle denied the accusations of possessing child sexual abuse material when they initially came to light, telling the Daily Mail they were untrue and "sick lies".
Meghan Markle, an American actor who married King Charles' younger son in 2018, has said she was "deeply distressed" by the allegations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Paraguayan President Pena impeached over banking crisis
Article:
ASUNCION: Paraguayan senators on Friday voted to impeach President Santiago Pena over the collapse of a major bank that locked almost half the population out of their accounts and triggered widespread protests.
Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that would strip him of the immunity granted to former presidents.
He did not attend the trial in the Senate despite earlier pledging to defend himself.
"The president is declared guilty of poor performance in his duties," Senate President Basilio Nunez declared after a vote of 44 in favour of impeachment, with one absence among the 45 senators.
Around three million people have been unable to access their money since the Central Bank took control of Ueno Bank on Tuesday and froze its accounts over concerns about its solvency.
A Central Bank official told AFP that advance payments to some affected depositors had begun on Thursday afternoon.
The bank's collapse brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno.
Lawmakers from Pena's own party backed his impeachment.
Pena, 47, apologised during an address to the nation on Thursday.
"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," he said in a video statement.
'Hurt'
Around 250 people gathered outside Congress awaiting the outcome of the trial, one of them waving a sign that read: "Pena in prison."
On Thursday, thousands protested for a third consecutive night in Asuncion and other cities to demand the return of their money.
"Santiago Pena has hurt so many Paraguayans, so many families, business owners and small business people, including my own son, who had savings in Ueno Bank," Cynthia Farina told AFP at a protest in the capital that police dispersed with tear gas and water cannon.
Advance payments to an unspecified number of affected depositors began on Thursday afternoon, Jose Maciel of the Central Bank's Deposit Guarantee Fund told AFP.
The first phase of aid deposits, of up to around US$1,600, will go to clients who do not have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, Maciel said.
The next beneficiaries "will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process", he said.
Ueno began as a small fintech company with a digital-first model that attracted low-income customers, rapidly becoming a major bank that handled state pensions and the accounts of several state entities.
The opposition accuses Pena of a conflict of interest, which he denies.
The attorney general said it was investigating him for "acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity".
The US Embassy in Paraguay expressed "its solidarity with the Paraguayan people" on Friday, without mentioning the president.
'Victims'
Ueno's downfall shocked the South American country, which is generally considered economically and politically stable.
By impeaching him rather than allowing him to resign, lawmakers have prevented Pena from becoming a senator for life and enjoying immunity from prosecution, constitutional experts and lawmakers told AFP.
Vice-President Pedro Alliana is preparing to complete the current mandate until 2028.
The scandal has claimed the heads of Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo and Interior Minister Enrique Riera.
Eight Ueno executives have been arrested.
Prosecutors on Friday raided the offices of technology company ITTI, which is part of Grupo Vazquez, confiscating hard drives, computers and other items.
"We found a large amount of documents that will be useful for the investigation," prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.
Nearby Argentina felt the impact of the crisis as some 1,000 ITTI employees were suspended for 30 days without pay.
Football also took a hit.
Ueno Bank sponsors several first-division teams as well as the national team.
"We were also victims of this situation," members of the national team said in a statement on X.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deepavali joy amid fading estate life
Article:
BENTONG: For much of the year, the oil palm plantation in  Jalan Karak-Manchis is a quiet place, its ageing community going about life far from the bustle of town.
But when Deepavali comes around, the stillness gives way to festive music, brightly lit homes and the crackle of fireworks as children and grandchildren return to celebrate the festival of lights.
For R. Gopal, 55, and his wife, S. Puspa Devi, 49, the celebration is less about the festivities than the joy of having their five children, aged between 21 and 28, under one roof again.
Born and raised on the estate, Gopal has watched the once-thriving plantation community gradually shrink as families retired, moved away and sought new lives elsewhere.
Yet Deepavali remains a cherished occasion, bringing a fleeting return of the warmth and camaraderie that once defined life on the estate.
"When I was young, more than 150 Indian families were living in the estate. Imagine how much fun we had. Now, only about 20 families remain, as many have retired and moved away.
"My wife and I eagerly look forward to Deepavali because that is when my eldest son, who works in Singapore, and his siblings return home. They usually spend about a week here before heading back to work," he told the
New Straits Times
.
The grandfather of five said most of the younger generation had left the plantation, many finding work outside Pahang.
These days, their homecomings are largely confined to Deepavali, the estate temple's annual festival or the funeral of a close family member.
For Gopal, the estate only truly comes alive when the children return, filling the neighbourhood with laughter and renewing friendships forged during their younger days.
"For older people like me, what matters most is spending the festive holidays with our children. They are the ones who bring the neighbourhood to life by decorating their homes, setting off firecrackers and playing festive music.
"On Deepavali morning, the entire estate community gathers at the temple within the plantation for prayers. Families dress in matching traditional outfits and greet one another.
"In the past, people would stay up until the early hours preparing special dishes, but these days, many prefer to have food catered," he said.
But beneath the festive cheer lies the quiet realisation that Gopal's own days on the estate are numbered.
With retirement just five years away, he knows that the Deepavali celebrations he has treasured since childhood may soon become memories of a place he once called home.
Like many of his former neighbours, he plans to leave the plantation after retirement, closing another chapter in a community that has steadily grown smaller over the decades.
"After retiring, many of my friends left the estate to live with their children. When I retire, my wife and I plan to move to Johor to stay with our son, but we will make an effort to return for the temple festival.
"Growing up on the estate is something I will always cherish. I often share stories with my grandchildren about my early days working here — living in the old wooden workers' quarters and how all my siblings would help my mother prepare muruku during Deepavali," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Bersatu welcomes PH despite no pact
Article:
MELAKA:  Bersatu has not issued any official directive to its grassroots to reciprocate support for Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates in the Melaka  election.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party nonetheless welcomed support from any party or voter intending to back its candidates.
"We welcome anyone who believes it is good to support Bersatu. We certainly appreciate it because we want our candidates to win.
"However, we have not issued any directives. Even so, Bersatu members understand what needs to be done," he said after a walkabout with residents at the Sungai Udang  constituency hall.
Muhyiddin was responding to reports on PH's readiness to assist the Bersatu machinery.
Earlier, Bersatu deputy president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu also confirmed no official directive was received by the party to do so.
Muhiyiddin then expressed appreciation for any open endorsement from supporters of other parties aimed at ensuring victory for Bersatu candidates.
He also confirmed there was no official cooperation between Bersatu and PH.
He said that early talks were held between party leaders to avoid seat overlaps.
Muhyiddin added that Bersatu remained open to working together with PH.
"Yes, we welcome it. We will not say we want to reject it," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azmin: Johor, Negri setbacks won't affect Bersatu in Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA:   Bersatu's failure to win  seats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan  elections does not necessarily reflect  voter support for the party in Melaka.
Its secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said the party acknowledged the risks but expected to reduce them through strategic planning and trained machinery.
He said the party's decision to contest seven seats was made after weighing various factors through strategic consideration and careful study.
"After giving it very careful and very thorough consideration, we feel the number that is significant and strategic enough for Bersatu this time is seven seats with the potential for us to win.
"Although we know that in any election there are risks, we have strategic planning and organised and trained machinery.
"So we are confident it can boost the support of the people of Melaka for Bersatu," he said in an interview  here.
Bersatu is fielding seven candidates,  whereas Wawasan is contesting two seats in Kesidang and Bemban under the PN logo.
Bersatu and Wawasan will also face off in Bemban, which will see a four-cornered fight that includes  Parti Bersama Malaysia and an independent.
Azmin said Bersatu was taking a different approach in this election by prioritising wisdom and suitable political strategy.
He said this included fielding candidates in state seats also contested by Pakatan Harapan, even though both sides were seen to have an understanding.
"It may be awkward because we have never been through a situation like this, but as I mentioned earlier, this is the wisdom of the political parties taking part in the Melaka election.
"Although there is cooperation, if they feel there is a winning factor or that victory favours them, then they will field a candidate there.
"But for Bersatu, based on other considerations, for example the candidate is well liked, accepted by voters, has an excellent record and is  young,  so we feel victory may favour Bersatu," he said.

Title: Cornell rape case exposes MeToo backlash
Article:
NEW YORK: An allegation of gang rape at the elite Cornell University horrified Americans. But when the alleged victim, known only as "Jane Doe", went public, she suffered a new kind of abuse, her lawyer told AFP.
The doxxing, threats and harassment targeting the woman, Thomas Giuffra said, expose a wider backlash against the MeToo movement, which prompted a societal reckoning with sexual abuse by men.
"I think we've gone the wrong way in how sexual assault is viewed in this country," said Giuffra, whose client claims that seven male students assaulted her at the Ivy League college in 2024.
"The message is to other survivors: Keep your mouth shut, or this is going to happen to you."
Giuffra cited a "swatting" incident in October in which police drew their guns at the woman's home after a man gave her address in a hoax call claiming to have shot his mother.
The lawyer also said he had received death threats.
"Somebody called my office and said 'drop the case, or I'm going to kill your wife'," he said in an interview at his 29th-floor Manhattan office.
Giuffra has previously represented accusers of Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced Hollywood mogul at the centre of abuse allegations that spurred the MeToo movement seeking to end impunity for sexual assault and rape.
"I thought we were moving in the right direction after MeToo, and there was just the backlash, and that set us back," he said, citing so-called "manosphere" influencers who oppose feminism.
In the Cornell backlash, he blamed "people who felt that the status quo was being threatened, people who didn't like the idea of women being treated equally, people who wanted to shut up women".
[[nid:1572580]]
'Brave woman'
Despite the intimidation, Giuffra said his client wanted her lawsuit to transform how Cornell and other US universities deal with sexual assault.
An estimated one in four female students experience rape or sexual assault at some point during their undergraduate studies, according to a 2020 study by the Association of American Universities.
Fraternities — male social clubs common on US campuses — are particularly scrutinised. The men accused in the Cornell case belonged to one, and the alleged gang rape took place at a fraternity house.
"It's not just about money; it's also about effectuating some kind of change," Giuffra said, adding that any settlement with Cornell would include steps to "protect, educate, support students".
"I think she wants her story to be: I made a difference," Giuffra said. "Jane doesn't want some other woman, if God forbid this happens to them, to be left on their own, thrown overboard like she was."
Cornell has already announced several preliminary reforms to support sexual assault victims and commissioned an independent probe into how it responded in 2024.
Following her initial allegations, Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the accused male students, two of whom were later expelled. Critics have said the response was too lenient.
On Friday, Cornell's faculty voted no-confidence in the university leadership.
New York's top prosecutor has also launched a fresh criminal investigation into the rape allegations after local authorities said they declined to prosecute in 2024 over a lack of evidence.
Giuffra praised the changes but said they were long overdue and inadequate. "There's an expression: that's a day late and a dollar short."
He said the accuser was still traumatised by her ordeal and had to take medication to help her sleep. Still, he praised her as a "brave woman".
"She's just trying to get through it every day at a time and trying to bring about some good," Giuffra said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Political canvassing amid a calm facade
Article:
MELAKA: Campaigning for the Melaka polls has so far been marked by a relatively cordial atmosphere on the ground, even as political parties sharpen their rhetoric and step up efforts to secure support ahead of polling day on Nov 14.
Campaign workers from Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan  and Perikatan Nasional have described the campaign as largely peaceful, with candidates concentrating on meeting voters, visiting communities and presenting their respective agendas.
Some have even likened the contest to a friendly football match, suggesting that political differences have yet to translate into open hostility among campaign teams.
A campaign worker for BN's Serkam candidate Datuk Azman Abdullah said there had been no provocations, describing the campaign as a healthy contest.
"There has been no provocations. Everything is fine, and we are competing in a healthy manner. It is like a friendly match of  football," he said.
He also claimed that some Pas supporters had expressed their intention to support Azman because they knew him personally, adding that the reception during house visits had been encouraging.
A PH campaign worker in Merlimau shared a similar assessment, saying candidates were focused on meeting people and visiting communities.
"There has been no provocation from rival parties because we regard this as a friendly match to choose the state's future leaders. The state election is a democratic process, and everyone is mature enough to carry out their responsibilities calmly," he said.
A PN Melaka media officer said he had received no complaints from the party's machinery about provocations, adding that cooperation between BN and PN supporters had improved, with both sides helping each other on the ground.
The coordination reflects efforts to translate the political understanding between the two coalitions into grassroots support, although local loyalties and competing interests could still pose challenges.
Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Communication and Media Studies senior lecturer Dr Siti Faidul Maisarah Abdullah said the campaign was calmer than the two previous  elections, with fewer controversies and party members displaying greater maturity and professionalism.
She also noted a change in campaign approaches, saying PH, which had appeared more aggressive in previous contests, was adopting a more persuasive approach this time.
Based on her observations, the authorities had been effective and committed in maintaining a harmonious atmosphere, which she said should be preserved until polling day.
Political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub similarly described the campaign as peaceful and orderly, with political competition yet to translate into widespread public hostility or major disturbances.
He said political intensity was nevertheless increasing, particularly in campaign rhetoric and on social media, although this had not resulted in widespread hostility or physical confrontations on the ground.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST CRIME WATCH: Sexual abuse, brawls and riots make headlines this week [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: At least 26 people were arrested following two riots in the Klang Valley, with police also seizing several weapons.
In Kuala Lumpur, more than 400 people were detained in raids at two entertainment outlets, one involving drug-related offences and the other the operation of an unlicensed entertainment centre.
In Jerantut, Pahang, a Standard One pupil was allegedly sexually abused by his teacher as punishment for failing to complete his homework.
Here are some of the major crime cases reported this week.
POLICE NAB 26 IN TWO SEPARATE RIOTS
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 17 people following
a brawl at the Lembah Jaya flats in Ampang
, after videos of the incident went viral on social media.
Police were dispatched to the scene just after 2am on Oct 31, but found the situation calm.
However, police arrested 17 men from a group that had gathered at the location. They were detained to assist in investigations.
They were remanded for between two and three days. The case is being investigated for rioting while armed with deadly weapons.
In a separate incident, nine people, including a woman, were arrested
following a riot outside a cafe
in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, Kuala Lumpur, believed to have been triggered by a dispute over business territory.
The suspects were aged between 16 and 44. Preliminary police investigations revealed that the clash stemmed from a misunderstanding over control of the business area.
Six of those arrested had previous criminal and drug-related records.
Police also seized several items believed to have been used in the fight and are tracking down about 15 other people.
TWO PARANG ATTACKS LEAVE ONE DEAD AND ANOTHER INJURED
PASIR GUDANG: A man was seriously injured after being attacked by a group of men armed with parang outside an apartment building in Taman Cendana, Pasir Gudang, Johor, just after midnight on Nov 2.
Jealousy was believed to be
the motive
behind the attack.
Police arrested a man in his 30s and seized a parang believed to have been used in the attack.
The victim was taken to Hospital Pasir Gudang and was reported to be in stable condition.
The suspect, who had a record of eight previous criminal and drug-related offences, also tested positive for methamphetamine.
Meanwhile, in Banting, Selangor, a man in his 20s died after being attacked by a group of men armed with parang.
The motive was believed to be revenge.
Three men in their 30s were arrested in the Banting area to assist in investigations.
Police are investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
TEACHER ARRESTED OVER SEXUAL ABUSE OF SEVEN-YEAR-OLD PUPIL
JERANTUT: A 24-year-old
male teacher was arrested
over allegations that he repeatedly sexually abused a seven-year-old pupil at a primary school here, including allegedly forcing the boy to perform oral sex as punishment for failing to complete his homework.
The alleged incidents reportedly took place in a science laboratory store.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob confirmed the arrest.
The case came to light after the boy disclosed the abuse to his family on Oct 27, prompting his father to lodge a police report.
The teacher was remanded for six days to facilitate investigations.
417 DETAINED IN NIGHTCLUB RAIDS
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 417 people during a raid on an unlicensed entertainment centre suspected of being linked to drug activities along Jalan Sultan Ismail here.
The raid was conducted on Nov 1 following intelligence that the premises was allegedly being used for drug-related activities.
Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those detained comprised security guards, workers and patrons, including four Bangladeshis.
The 417, comprising 299 men and 118 women, were taken to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters for documentation and urine screening.
In a separate operation conducted on the same day, police arrested eight men, aged between 21 and 40, at another unlicensed entertainment centre along Jalan Tun Razak.
Wangsa Maju police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said those arrested comprised six foreigners, including two Bangladeshis and two Myanmar nationals without valid travel documents, as well as two Chinese nationals.
Police also seized audio equipment, four bottles of liquor and business sales receipts worth more than RM2,100.
THREE REMANDED FOR GIVING BRIBES IN CIGARETTE-SMUGGLING RING
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) arrested three people, including a businessman with the title Datuk, for allegedly offering about RM1 million in bribes to police in exchange for protection for illegal cigarette-smuggling activities.
The suspects comprised a company owner and two women – a tuition teacher and a marketing executive – aged between their 30s and 50s.
They were arrested on Nov 1 at separate locations in Putrajaya, Selangor and Johor.
Preliminary investigations found that the suspects allegedly conspired to offer bribes to several police officers and lower-ranking policemen to prevent enforcement action against cigarette-smuggling activities in the East Coast states and the Klang Valley.
The alleged arrangement was believed to have been in operation since 2020, with the suspects also suspected of acting as intermediaries to channel the money to the police personnel involved.
MACC seized four luxury vehicles worth about RM600,000, four mobile phones and a laptop. It also froze 20 personal bank accounts and nine company accounts containing RM1.5 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST COURT WATCH: Rape acquittal, faith rehabilitation order among key court cases this week [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An acquittal in a rape case, an order to undergo faith rehabilitation, fines for illegal racing under newly amended laws and unsuccessful court bids were among the court cases that made headlines across the country this week.
In Putrajaya, celebrity preacher Da'i Syed became a free man after succeeding in his final appeal against his rape conviction.
In Kuala Lumpur, a Taiwanese karaoke centre manager was charged with driving under the influence of drugs after allegedly crashing his car into a police escort rider attached to the entourage of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Also in Kuala Lumpur, Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid, widow of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, failed in her suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over a police probe into an alleged plot to topple the government.
Here are several court cases that made headlines this week.
PREACHER DA'I SYED WINS APPEAL
Celebrity preacher Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, was
cleared of raping a 23-year-old woman
in Shah Alam in 2019.
In a 2-1 majority decision, Court of Appeal judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowed Syed Shah Iqmal's final appeal, while Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid dissented.
The bench set aside the 10-year jail term and three strokes of the rotan imposed by the High Court.
Azman said the defence had succeeded in raising reasonable doubt, rendering Syed Shah Iqmal's conviction unsafe.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to raping the woman in a condominium in i-City, Section 7, on Sept 11, 2019.
The charge, framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
In 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted him after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case.
However, the Shah Alam High Court allowed the prosecution's appeal and ordered him to enter his defence.
On Aug 30, 2024, Sessions Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid sentenced him to 10 years in jail and three strokes of the rotan.
TAIWANESE MAN CHARGED OVER CRASH THAT INJURED POLICEMAN
Taiwanese karaoke centre manager Wei Fu-Chun, 52, pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court to driving a Mercedes-Benz
under the influence of drugs
and crashing into Corporal Samsul Rahimi Sapari, 42, who sustained injuries to his legs and hands.
The offence took place at 8.50pm along Jalan Tun Sambanthan on Oct 31.
He was charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
Samsul, who is attached to the city Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department's motorcycle unit, was returning from escort duty with the entourage of Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar denied Wei bail and fixed Jan 6 for the submission of documents.
A breathalyser test conducted on Wei returned a negative result for alcohol, but drugs believed to be ecstasy were found in the car.
NA'IMAH AND SONS' SUIT AGAINST PRIME MINISTER STRUCK OUT
The originating summons filed by Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid, her two sons and two lawyers
challenging police investigations
into an alleged plot to topple the government was struck out by the High Court.
The suit was filed by Na'imah, widow of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, alongside Amir Zainuddin, Amin Zainuddin and lawyers Amir Zharif Abdullah and Muhammad Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Mohd Khalid Ismail and the government were named as the defendants.
Judge Indra Nehru Savandiah ruled that there was no cogent evidence to substantiate allegations that the police investigation was conducted in bad faith or with mala fide intentions.
She said the allegations that the ongoing police investigation might have been influenced by the first defendant's alleged public comments were merely assertions or assumptions unsupported by facts capable of establishing bad faith or mala fide intentions.
She also said there was no nexus linking the first defendant's alleged public comments to the independent ongoing investigation, which was based on a police report.
The plaintiffs contended that the investigation under Section 124B of the Penal Code for activities detrimental to parliamentary democracy constituted an abuse of statutory power and was initiated in bad faith.
They sought, among other things, a declaration that the investigation by the IGP and the government under Section 124B was unlawful, unconstitutional, tainted with bad faith, carried out for ulterior purposes and an abuse of statutory power.
MAN ORDERED TO UNDERGO THREE MONTHS OF FAITH REHABILITATION
A man who went viral for performing a non-Islamic ritual was ordered by the Syariah Lower Court to undergo three months of faith rehabilitation after pleading guilty to a charge of improper worship.
Syariah judge Mohd Faizal Habib ordered Aliff Daniel Adli, 21, to
undergo rehabilitation
at the Baitul Iman Faith Rehabilitation Centre in Ulu Yam instead of serving a jail term or paying a fine.
Aliff admitted to committing improper worship by holding a religious object, performing a ritual involving body piercing and kneeling with both hands clasped against his chest in front of a statue.
The offence took place at a temple in Batu Caves between 9pm and 11pm on Jan 24, 2024.
The court reprimanded Aliff, saying the offence was not merely a breach of written law but a serious transgression. It also advised him to repent.
SINGAPOREAN AMONG THREE FINED FOR ILLEGAL RACING
Singaporean national serviceman Syajahan Alfian Abdullah was fined RM3,500 by the Johor Bahru magistrate's court for riding a motorcycle at high speed and
taking part in a speed challenge
.
The charge was brought against Syajahan, 19, under Section 42A(2) of the amended Road Transport Act 1987 (Amendment) 2026, which criminalises illegal racing and speed testing on public roads. The amendments came into force on Oct 16.
He pleaded guilty to committing the act at Km12.5 of the Second Link Expressway southbound in Iskandar Puteri at 2.10am on Oct 18.
Two other local youths, Muhammad Daniel Hakim Mohamad Rashid, 24, and Gonzales Mckhovic George, 18, were also fined RM3,500 each after pleading guilty to offences under Section 42A(1) for racing their motorcycles along different stretches of the same expressway at the same time and date.
The amended provisions carry a fine of between RM2,000 and RM10,000, a jail term of up to two years, or both, for a first offence.
The three paid their fines.
CAPRICE ORDERED TO PAY PREACHER EBIT LEW RM220,000 FOR DEFAMATION
The Shah Alam Sessions Court ordered rapper and influencer Ariz Ramli, better known as Caprice, to pay preacher
Ebit Lew
RM220,000 in damages for defamation.
On Nov 2, judge Zuhrina Mohamed Nor ordered Caprice to deposit the sum into the account of Ebit's lawyers and pay RM2,000 in costs after dismissing his application to stay the payment.
In August, the judge had ordered Caprice to apologise and pay Ebit RM220,000 after finding that he had defamed the preacher in 2023.
Caprice was also ordered to remove seven statements made alongside Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo within 48 hours and barred from making further comments or statements about Ebit.
The case stemmed from a video Caprice uploaded on Sept 15, 2023, featuring Mondy as a guest.
Ebit said the video implied that he had sexually harassed and taken advantage of Mondy, portraying him as irresponsible and someone who exploited religion.

Title: Cornell faculty vote no-confidence in leadership over alleged gang rape
Article:
NEW YORK: Faculty members at Cornell University on Friday passed a no-confidence vote over how the elite college's leadership handled an alleged gang rape that has sparked outcry in the United States.
The result is not binding but marks a strong symbolic rebuke of administrators following the 2024 incident, which saw a female student assaulted by seven male students on campus, according to a lawsuit.
Critics have accused Cornell of being too lenient in its initial response.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump elevates hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff after midterm defeat
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump named trusted aide Stephen Miller as his chief of staff on Friday, giving the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies one of the most powerful jobs in Washington after Republicans lost control of Congress.
Miller, who will replace Susie Wiles, assumes the role as the president prepares to confront a Democratic-led House of Representatives and Senate, as well as a wave of congressional investigations into his administration.
A longtime proponent of expansive presidential authority, Miller takes over at a moment when the Republican Party's defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections could leave Trump more reliant on executive power to advance his domestic agenda.
In a social media post, Trump called Miller "one of my most trusted advisers" and praised Wiles for doing "an outstanding job". Trump said the change would take effect on Monday.
A White House official said Miller's appointment signalled that Trump had no intention of rethinking his policies and was instead rewarding his most loyal aides.
"He's not changing course," the official said, despite tens of millions of American voters repudiating Trump's domestic agenda and foreign policy this week.
While Trump said this week he was willing to work with Democrats on Capitol Hill, the elevation of Miller, known for being uncompromising, could suggest a more confrontational approach and a push to advance the president's agenda, several White House officials said.
Trump had been displeased with his political and communications operations in the run-up to Tuesday's election as his public approval ratings fell to near-record lows. This week, he said the White House needed to be "more aggressive" as Democrats retake congressional power, according to a person briefed on the matter.
Miller drove immigration crackdown
Miller, 41, is one of Trump's longest-serving aides and is among the few who served throughout his first and second terms in office.
