Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially served as deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he has wielded outsize influence across much of Trump's domestic agenda and has had the president's ear.
He is perhaps best known for driving Trump's aggressive immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests a day. In pursuit of that target, federal immigration agents expanded their list of targets to include migrants who had been living in the US for decades.
He was also deeply involved in Trump's campaign to remake the federal bureaucracy, which led to the dismissal of tens of thousands of civil servants in 2025. He was also a driving force behind the administration's battles with universities, diversity programmes and other institutions.
Hakeem Jeffries, who is set to become the new Democratic speaker of the House, responded to the announcement of Miller's promotion by calling him a "reckless extremist" in a post on X.
Shake-up after election setback
The chief of staff typically wields great influence as the president's gatekeeper. The person manages White House staff, organises the president's time and schedule, and maintains contact with other government departments and lawmakers.
Wiles, 69, who submitted her resignation on Thursday night, will move to Trump's political operation, according to a White House official.
The veteran political operative from Florida was the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff.
She brought decades of political experience to the role and was regarded as running a more disciplined operation than some of Trump's previous top aides. She maintained her role even while undergoing treatment earlier this year for early-stage breast cancer.
Wiles rarely challenged Trump's policies but brought discipline to an often chaotic operation and was seen as a voice of reason. Her exit raises questions about who will play her role.
Trump went through four chiefs of staff — an unusually high number — during his 2017-2021 term, as they were seen to have struggled to rein in the unpredictable president.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France's top literary prize winner defends 'playful' use of AI
Article:
PARIS: The winner of France's top literary award, the Prix Goncourt, defended on Friday his "playful", "ironic" and very limited use of AI in his acclaimed book.
"It is ridiculously absurd to think for half a second that I used generative AI to write anything at all in this book," Philippe Jaenada said in a statement sent to AFP by his publisher, Flammarion, in which the author detailed how he used the technology.
"The playful or ironic use of AI — above all fully acknowledged — was actually part of my plan even before I started writing," he said.
Jaenada, who was announced on Tuesday as the winner of the 2026 prize for his novel "L'Inconnue du quai de Javel" (The Unknown Woman of the Quai de Javel), had admitted to using AI three times during the writing process.
His comments came amid a worldwide backlash against academics and authors, including their exclusion from literary competitions, over allegations of using the technology in their writing.
On Friday, Jaenada reiterated that he had used AI only three times for his sprawling novel about the unsolved murder of a young Breton woman in the late 1940s.
First, the author asked a question to AI chatbots and said he received "comically precise, and therefore stupid, and contradictory answers".
He then used AI in a more conventional way, to conduct research.
Finally, he said he amused himself by "hiding in the text a sentence generated by AI".
It amounted to just 10 words, and since the book's publication, he had received dozens of guesses from readers.
The writer said he had decided to reveal the sentence in response to "stupidity, treachery, and bad faith".
Once considered a frontrunner for the Prix Goncourt, Haitian-Canadian author Thelyson Orelien had his novel withdrawn from the shortlist amid speculation that he had used AI to write it.
Orelien's Canadian publisher last month confirmed that he had used AI to help write the book and was severing professional ties with the author.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: French death blaze holiday home owner to face trial
Article:
PARIS: The owner of a French holiday home where 11 people died in a fire in 2023 will face trial for involuntary manslaughter and involuntary bodily harm, prosecutors said on Friday.
The victims of the fire in the small town of Wintzenheim in the Alsace region of eastern France were 10 adults with learning disabilities and their companion, on a break during the peak of the French summer holiday season.
The holiday home owner and a management company of which she is the sole shareholder will face the charges, Paris prosecutors said.
The trial is expected to take place from Jan 25 to Feb 10.
Local authorities said the building, a former barn renovated a few years earlier, had not been properly declared or brought into compliance with regulations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman arrested after driver swap precedes PLUS crash that killed retired cop, wife near Kuala Muda
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — A 36-year-old woman has been arrested after a retired policeman and his wife were killed when their scooter collided with a car that had pulled out of the emergency lane following a driver swap.
Police are investigating whether the woman, who owns the Perodua Bezza, was driving or a passenger when the crash occurred on the North-South Expressway near Kuala Muda yesterday.
According to
Sinar Harian
, Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the woman was detained to help establish the circumstances surrounding the collision.
The crash occurred at about noon at KM114.4 of the expressway, killing retired police sergeant Suhaimi Saidin, 64, and his wife Normah Hashim, 60.
The couple, who were travelling home to Bandar Utama on a Yamaha XMAX scooter, suffered severe head and body injuries and died at the scene.
Preliminary investigations indicate that the Bezza had stopped in the emergency lane before rejoining the left lane after its occupants switched drivers.
The couple’s scooter and another motorcycle subsequently collided with the car.
Two teenagers riding the second motorcycle were injured and taken to Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital for treatment.
“Initial information indicates that the vehicle had stopped and moved again after switching drivers,” Hanyan said.
“We are investigating whether she was driving or was a passenger at the time of the impact. The arrest is necessary to facilitate further inquiries.”
Police have appealed for witnesses, particularly motorists with dashcam footage of the crash, to come forward to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Title: Palestinian PM’s adviser calls for deeper Malaysia cooperation in development, diplomacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Palestine hopes to deepen cooperation with Malaysia through concrete projects and programmes to support the country’s development and economy towards the realisation of the State of Palestine, Advisor to the Palestinian Prime Minister for International Relations Izzat Abdel Hadi said.
He said Malaysia could play a greater role in strengthening Palestinian institutions and the economy through technical cooperation and investment, as well as use its expertise in various sectors to contribute to capacity-building efforts, particularly in areas such as healthcare, education, and community infrastructure.
“Malaysia can also assist through humanitarian support, particularly in Gaza, including healthcare, education and community infrastructure,” he said during an interview on Bernama TV’s
The Nation
programme,
Palestine Beyond The Headlines: Rebuilding Under Occupation
, recently.
He also highlighted opportunities for closer economic cooperation, including in the halal sector, which could benefit both countries.
Abdel Hadi said Malaysia’s standing within Asean and the international community could also help amplify Palestinian concerns and strengthen diplomatic support for Palestinian rights and statehood.
“On the diplomatic level, I think we can also utilise Malaysia’s membership in Asean and their diplomatic influence within Asean and other international fora to support the Palestinian rights and realisation of the Palestinian state, and to promote international law,” he said.
He also expressed appreciation for Malaysia’s continued solidarity with Palestine, including the unwavering support demonstrated by the country’s leadership and people. — Bernama

Title: Saifullizan Ishak named new Sarawak police chief, Zailanni Amit appointed deputy
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 7 — DCP Saifullizan Ishak has been promoted to Commissioner of Police (CP) and appointed Sarawak’s new police chief.
In a Facebook post on its official page, Polis Sarawak, the Sarawak Contingent Police Headquarters announced that DCP Zailanni Amit would replace him as Sarawak deputy police commissioner.
“Indeed, these promotions and appointments are a most meaningful recognition of the dedication, commitment, experience and meritorious service rendered throughout their careers in the Royal Malaysia Police.
“They are not merely a career achievement, but also a trust and a great responsibility demanding wisdom, firmness and leadership of integrity,” the post read.
Saifullizan previously served as acting Sarawak police commissioner following the transfer of his predecessor, Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, to Bukit Aman, where he assumed the post of management director last month.
Hailing from Kedah, Saifullizan, 56, had also held various posts throughout his 31-year service with the police since 1995 — including chief assistant director for integrity, Special Branch chief assistant director, security liaison officer for the High Commission of Malaysia in Singapore, and investigating officer.
He holds a Master of Social Science in Policing Studies from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), a Diploma in Investigative Science from Universiti Malaya (UM), and is a Certified Integrity Officer (CeIO). — The Borneo Post

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB expects 7,000 visitors at Deepavali Open House on Nov 14
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 7 — About 7,000 visitors are expected to attend the Negeri Sembilan-level Deepavali Open House at the Seremban City Council (MBS) Hall on November 14, from 11am to 4pm.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the state government had also increased its allocation for this year’s Deepavali Carnival to RM70,000 from RM30,000 last year.
He said a variety of dishes representing the diversity of the state’s communities and cultures, particularly traditional Indian cuisine, would be served at the event, allowing visitors to enjoy an array of food in a spirit of goodwill and harmony.
“The state government invites all Negeri Sembilan residents to attend the Deepavali celebration in large numbers to foster goodwill among the communities.
“Our aim is to ensure that every celebration is held in a lively, harmonious and joyful atmosphere, strengthening ties among the communities and further reinforcing the unity that has already been established,” he told reporters after officiating the 2026 Deepavali Carnival here.
Ismail said allocations had also been channelled to rural areas, including estates, to ensure that programmes and the distribution of contributions in conjunction with Deepavali could benefit needy members of the Indian community.
“We want to ensure that no one is left out from receiving the assistance and facilities provided by the state government,” he said.
In a separate development, he said the proposal to gazette Jalan Dato Lee Fong Yee as Seremban’s Little India would be discussed in detail with the Seremban City Council mayor before any decision was made.
He said the area, which had previously been known among the local community as Little India, had the potential to be developed into one of the state’s tourist attractions. — Bernama

Title: HR Ministry: Ramanan’s appeal seeks legal clarity, not an end to NUBE-MCBA negotiations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The continuation of Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan’s appeal in the dispute between the National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) and the Malaysian Commercial Banks’ Association (MCBA) is aimed at obtaining a Court of Appeal ruling on legal issues arising from the High Court’s decision, the ministry said today.
In a statement, the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) said the continuation of the appeal did not mean the ministry was closing the door to an amicable settlement through negotiations between the two parties.
“The human resources minister (Ramanan) did not apply for a stay of execution of the High Court’s decision, while the Department of Industrial Relations Malaysia had taken proactive steps by summoning the parties involved to resume conciliation proceedings.
“However, MCBA exercised its right to apply for a stay of execution of the High Court’s decision, and the application was granted by the Court,” Kesuma said.
The statement added that the stay order had prevented negotiations on the collective agreement from proceeding for as long as the order remained in force.
In this regard, Kesuma clarified that Ramanan’s withdrawal of the appeal would not automatically allow negotiations between NUBE and MCBA to resume, as the stay order obtained by MCBA remained in force.
Kesuma also reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating the resolution of industrial disputes through dialogue and amicable negotiations, in line with legal provisions and the principles of industrial harmony.
The ministry also urged all parties to respect the ongoing legal process and remain open to an amicable settlement, subject to the Court’s orders, in order to safeguard the rights and interests of all parties.
The media had previously reported that the dispute between MCBA and NUBE involved the payment of festive assistance and the 20th Collective Agreement.
On February 13, the High Court allowed NUBE’s application for judicial review, quashed two references made by the Human Resources Minister to the Industrial Court and directed both parties to resume negotiations.
However, on September 26, the High Court allowed MCBA’s application to stay the execution of the decision pending the association’s appeal at the Court of Appeal. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Malaysia eyes shift in internet coverage measurements to include key economic areas
Article:
DOHA, Nov 7 — Malaysia intends to propose at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) level that internet coverage measurements should no longer focus solely on the Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) standard, but should also take into account areas where economic activities take place.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposal was being studied following complaints from members of the public and Members of Parliament about internet connectivity problems in locations without residential settlements but which serve as major transportation routes or economic activity centres.
He said the existing approach, which is based on coverage in populated areas, should be reconsidered by taking into account the concept of Coverage of Economic Areas to ensure that connectivity needs in economic areas were also given due attention.
“We want to propose at the ITU level whether it would be appropriate to reconsider the standard from COPA to Coverage of Economic Areas. We want to look beyond whether people live in a particular area and consider whether economic activities are being carried out there,” he said in an interview ahead of the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) here today.
Fahmi said areas that warranted attention included major roads, railway lines, ports, coastal areas used by fishermen, as well as tourism and recreational destinations.
He said these areas might not have permanent residents but still required good internet access to support economic activities and the movement of people.
“Many have complained about internet connectivity or their network coverage along major routes, roads and places that do not have residents but serve as links between two locations or host economic activities,” he said.
Fahmi said recreational areas such as Taman Negara and the islands in Sabah were also among the locations that warranted consideration in internet coverage planning, as they supported economic activities despite not necessarily being residential areas.
He said the proposal had the potential to broaden the approach to assessing digital connectivity needs, particularly in areas that played an important role in economic activities.
“We see a lot of need to take forward ideas such as this, which have not been discussed so far. So, Malaysia could perhaps be among the first to bring this matter to the ITU level,” he said.
Fahmi is in Doha from November 6 to 11 to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26, with the mission of retaining the country’s seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
Malaysia’s participation in the ITU’s highest-level conference, held every four years, also aims to ensure that the country’s voice and interests continue to be represented in discussions on the global direction of telecommunications and information and communications technology (ICT) development.
The move reflects the country’s aspiration to remain actively involved in international strategic discussions, not merely keeping abreast of global technological developments but also contributing to shaping their direction.
Malaysia’s position on the council also provides an opportunity for the country to share its experience and approaches in addressing connectivity challenges, particularly in telecommunications infrastructure development.
Apart from strengthening diplomatic ties, the membership would also enhance Malaysia’s international visibility and reinforce its role in digital cooperation, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.
The ITU is a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for information and communications technology (ICT) matters, including standardisation, radio spectrum allocation and coordination of global telephone and satellite connections, as well as efforts to bridge the digital divide worldwide. — Bernama

Title: LTAT launches five-year anti-corruption plan to safeguard military retirement funds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) yesterday launched its Ethics, Transparency, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy (SETIA) 2026-2030 to strengthen good governance practices and ensure the sustainability of the retirement funds of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel.
LTAT said the launch of the five-year strategic plan followed its successful completion of all 30 initiatives under the 2022-2026 Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan (OACP), representing a 100 per cent achievement rate.
According to LTAT, SETIA marks the next phase in its ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional integrity, enhance accountability and foster ethical practices across all aspects of its operations and investment decisions.
“As an institution entrusted with managing the retirement savings of MAF personnel, LTAT believes that integrity and good governance are essential foundations for protecting contributors’ interests, while ensuring that every responsibility is carried out with full transparency,” it said in a statement yesterday.
The launch ceremony, held in conjunction with the 2026 International Anti-Corruption Day celebrations, was attended by LTAT Chairman Gen (Rtd) Tan Sri Azizan Ariffin, LTAT Chief Executive Datuk Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi, Deputy Secretary-General of the Treasury and LTAT Integrity Committee Chairman Datuk Shahrazat Ahmad, and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Community Education Division director Datuk Hairuzam Mohmad Amin @ Hamim.
The SETIA implementation framework comprises five strategic pillars and 25 initiatives specifically designed to strengthen corruption risk management, enhance transparency and reinforce accountability at all levels of the organisation over the long term.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Ashraf, in his keynote address, said every investment decision, expenditure and management action must be firmly guided by the principles of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
“The trust placed in LTAT by MAF personnel is a tremendous responsibility, as we are entrusted with protecting their interests and the future that has been placed in our care,” he said.
He acknowledged that LTAT had faced various challenges in the past, some of which had tested public confidence in the institution’s governance, but said these experiences had served as valuable lessons to prevent a recurrence.
“We cannot change the past, but we can and must ensure that the past does not determine the direction of our future. LTAT will not compromise on any misconduct, abuse of power or breach of ethical standards,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Boy, 11, drowns after falling into river while fishing with friends in Subang Perdana
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — A group of children’s joyful fishing outing in a river near Desa Subang Perantau 2, Subang Perdana here ended in tragedy when one of them was found drowned yesterday afternoon.
Selangor Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the victim who died was an 11-year-old Indonesian boy.
He said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 3:28pm before 11 personnel from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) were dispatched to the scene in Jalan Ikhlas.
“The search operation for the victim was also assisted by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from BBP Pelabuhan Klang and BBP Shah Alam.
“Based on initial information from the victim’s friends at the location, the victim fell into the river while they were fishing,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Ashrul Riezal said the victim was subsequently found at the riverbank in an unconscious state at 5:10pm and was pronounced dead by the Ministry of Health, before his body was handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Austria seek closer ties ahead of 65 years of diplomatic relations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Austria and Malaysia are committed to further strengthening bilateral relations in various fields, including foreign policy, regional cooperation, trade, investment, education, and culture, as both countries prepare to celebrate 65 years of diplomatic relations next year.
Austrian Ambassador to Malaysia Gerhard Eisl said the two countries shared common values and were like-minded partners on various international issues, particularly in promoting peace, dialogue, multilateralism, and international cooperation.
“Malaysia is an important partner for Austria. We are like-minded in many fields. Our relations are excellent at multilateral level, where we closely cooperate, for example on disarmament and nuclear non-proliferation, but also bilaterally,” he said at Austria’s National Day reception here yesterday.
Also present was Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Expressing confidence in the continued friendship between the two nations, Eisl said both countries were peace-loving nations strategically located at the centre of their respective regions, with Austria in the heart of Europe and Malaysia in the midst of Southeast Asia.
“Austria and Malaysia are deepening their relations in many areas, from foreign policy to regional cooperation, also in the framework of Asean, business, universities to culture,” he said, noting that several initiatives were being prepared to commemorate the 65th anniversary celebrations.
He also described Malaysia as an important market for Austrian businesses, noting that trade and investment remained the backbone of bilateral relations. He thanked Austrian companies operating in Malaysia for their contributions to strengthening economic ties.
Meanwhile, Eisl highlighted Austria’s commitment to international peace and security, recalling the country’s declaration of permanent neutrality on October 26, 1955, which was subsequently enshrined in its constitution.
“This decision, enshrined in our constitution, means military neutrality, not indifference. Austria stands for international law and human rights. We are a country of peace, dialogue and trust,” he said.
He noted that Austria’s commitment to taking greater responsibility in international affairs had become increasingly important amid the resurgence of power politics, wars, and armed conflicts that were putting the rules-based international order under pressure.
In this regard, Eisl expressed appreciation for Malaysia’s support for Austria’s candidature as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) for the 2027-2028 term, alongside 130 other UN member states.
“Thanks to the support of 131 UN member states, including Malaysia, Austria has been elected as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the period 2027-2028,” he said.
He said Austria would use its position to champion multilateralism and represent the interests of smaller and medium-sized countries, while giving a stronger voice to vulnerable communities, particularly civilians and children affected by armed conflicts.
“In the UN Security Council, Austria will be a reliable partner, a strong voice for multilateralism, a voice especially of the smaller and medium-sized countries, and a voice of those who need our protection most, especially civilians in armed conflicts, foremost children,” he said. — Bernama

Title: One dead, six injured in Proton Ertiga–Honda Civic collision in Kluang
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 7 — An elderly man was killed while six others sustained minor injuries in a collision involving a Proton Ertiga multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) and a Honda Civic at Jalan Ladang Sindora towards Ulu Belitong, Renggam here yesterday afternoon.
Renggam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Ramli Said said the department received an emergency call at 3.38pm and dispatched six firefighters and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) to the scene.
Firefighters extricated the victims from the MPV, whose driver, a man in his 60s, was pronounced dead at the scene, he said in a statement yesterday.
“Three other occupants of the Proton Ertiga, aged between eight and 54, sustained minor injuries, while the Honda Civic driver and two passengers, who were family members, also sustained minor injuries.
“Firefighters provided initial treatment to the injured victims before handing them over to the Health Ministry for further treatment, while the body of the deceased was handed over to the police,” he said.
The rescue operation ended at 5.45pm. — Bernama

Title: MACC looking for Toh Lean Seng, 53, to assist in money laundering investigation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in a money laundering investigation.
The MACC said the individual, identified as Toh Lean Seng, is 53 years old, adding that efforts to locate the man at his last known address at 15-1 231, TR Service Apartment, 231 Jalan Tun Razak, 50490 Kuala Lumpur, were unsuccessful.
“The investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
“Anyone who knows or has information about this individual is urged to contact the investigating officer, PsK Mohd Shokray Yahaya, at 019-6236680 or via email at mohdshokray@sprm.gov.my,” the commission said in a statement last night. — Bernama

Title: Penang police probe viral video alleging officers took money during roadside check
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Police are conducting a thorough investigation into a viral video circulating on social media alleging misconduct by police personnel while carrying out law enforcement duties at Puncak Erskine, Jalan Fettes, in Tanjung Tokong here.
Northeast District Police Chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police detected the video yesterday following its circulation on social media, which had attracted public attention.
“A police report has been lodged by the officer involved, who denied the allegation of corruption during the inspection.
“Following this, police are conducting a thorough investigation into the incident depicted in the viral video under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998,” he said in a statement last night.
He said the investigation would also look into whether the police personnel involved had complied with procedures and disciplinary regulations.
He also advised the public against sharing the video or making any speculation that could affect the investigation. Witnesses, individuals involved and anyone with information about the incident are urged to assist the investigation by contacting the Northeast District Police Headquarters at 04-2181822 or the investigating officer, Insp Zahirrudin Ismail, at 014-3189026.
Earlier, several videos went viral on social media showing two police personnel from a mobile patrol unit stopping a car carrying several individuals and conducting checks on them. The person recording the video alleged that the officers had taken money from the group. — Bernama

Title: Landslide forces full closure of Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor stretch after heavy rain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — A landslide following heavy rain yesterday has resulted in the full closure of a section of Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor (B27) at Section 9.90 in the Gombak district.
The Selangor Public Works Department (JKR) said the landslide, which occurred at 11 pm, involved failures of both the upslope and downslope, causing part of the road structure at the affected section to collapse.
The agency said the landslide also brought down trees, blocking the entire road to traffic.
“The road closure was implemented by the Gombak District JKR, while information on alternative routes was disseminated to road users through the Facebook pages of JKR Selangor and Gombak District JKR yesterday morning.
“The incident is believed to have been caused by heavy rain, which resulted in a high volume of rainwater infiltration and increased soil saturation in the sloping area,” the department said in a media statement last night.
The department said the resulting increase in pore water pressure subsequently caused slope instability and soil movement, leading to the collapse and damage of part of the road structure.
However, Selangor JKR said detailed investigations and technical assessments were still underway to determine the actual cause of the incident.
In addition, a Traffic Management Plan (TMP), including the installation of full road closure and diversion signs, had been activated, while temporary tarpaulin sheets had been installed over the affected road embankment and slope surfaces to prevent erosion and further landslides.
“Clearing works to remove soil debris and fallen trees from the upslope area have been carried out by the state road concessionaire, alongside continuous monitoring of active movement in the road structure and slope stability,” the department said.
A temporary diversion road would be constructed in the affected area for light vehicles, subject to technical considerations involving safety and slope stability.
“Announcements on the reopening of the road will be made once technical assessments confirm that it is safe for traffic, and a diversion route restricted to light vehicles has been provided,” it said. — Bernama

Title: MMEA seizes RM8m worth of vessels, items over suspected illegal cargo transfer off Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Two vessels and other items with an estimated total value of RM8 million were seized by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Penang waters on Thursday for allegedly carrying out cargo transfer activities without a valid licence.
In a statement today, Penang MMEA director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the vessels, a tugboat and an unregistered sampan, were detained at 11.40am following information received and public complaints.
He said an initial inspection found that the vessels were allegedly involved in transferring cargo from the sampan to the tugboat without a valid cargo licence as required under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance (MSO) 1952.
Those detained comprised two Vietnamese nationals, who were the tugboat’s master and chief engineer, and a local man who was the sampan skipper, along with the vessels, related documents and other seized items, all of which were handed over to MMEA investigating officers for further investigation.
Muhammad Suffi said compliance with maritime laws and licensing conditions was essential to ensuring navigational safety, orderly shipping activities and the protection of national interests. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia seeks early date for Anwar-Prabowo talks as bilateral agreements await signing
Article:
JAKARTA, Nov 7 — Efforts will be made to convene the Malaysia-Indonesia Annual Consultation at the earliest opportunity, with several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) already agreed upon for signing during the high-level meeting.
Malaysian Ambassador to Indonesia Datuk Muzafar Shah Mustafa said he had raised the matter directly with President Prabowo Subianto during an interaction at Istana Merdeka on Friday, following the presentation of his credentials to the Indonesian leader.
“Overall, I view President Prabowo’s remarks as very positive, and I hope this will provide further momentum to strengthen the good relations between Malaysia and Indonesia,” he told Bernama.
The upcoming 14th Annual Consultation will bring together Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Prabowo to review bilateral cooperation and discuss issues of mutual interest.
The Annual Consultation is the highest-level bilateral mechanism between the two countries, providing a platform for their leaders to advance cooperation in trade, investment, defence, security, border matters, and other strategic areas.
The previous consultation, the 13th in the series, was held in Jakarta on July 29, 2025, marking the revival of the mechanism after the last meeting in Kuching, Sarawak, in 2017.
Muzafar said he also conveyed greetings from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and Anwar to Prabowo, while reaffirming Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with Indonesia as a neighbour and strategic partner.
“President Prabowo repeatedly emphasised that Malaysia and Indonesia are brotherly nations. He also spoke about his close relationship with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, whom he described as a former schoolmate, as well as his close ties with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim,” he said.
The Indonesian President also emphasised the close cultural and people-to-people ties between the two countries and expressed hope that bilateral relations would continue to grow.
Malaysia and Indonesia will commemorate the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027, marking seven decades of bilateral ties since the establishment of formal ties in 1957.
On forest and land fires, Muzafar said Prabowo emphasised that Indonesia had done its utmost to tackle the problem, including mobilising tens of thousands of personnel and deploying various firefighting assets.
He said Prabowo also referred to companies including those from Malaysia and Singapore, and stressed that firm action would be taken against those found to have committed offences. — Bernama

Title: Deepavali Carnival at Bukit Jalil attracts nearly 200,000 visitors, gives 700 entrepreneurs business boost, says Ramanan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The 24th Deepavali Carnival at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil near here, which attracted nearly 200,000 visitors, including foreign tourists, proves the event is not merely a festive shopping venue but also a platform to spur local businesses.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the encouraging response to the nine-day carnival, which began October 30, gave 700 entrepreneurs an opportunity to expand their market reach and boost sales.
He said that, based on his observation, business activities at participating stalls showed positive growth.
“Preparations have indeed been good. I visited the stalls here, and their sales have been very good. I understand that this is the 24th time this carnival has been held.
“Some visitors came from Medan, Singapore and Australia. Sometimes they come here just as tourists to visit Malaysia, but after attending this carnival, they return repeatedly,” he told reporters after visiting the carnival yesterday.
Ramanan said the government is also prepared to look into suitable support and assistance to empower entrepreneurs participating in the carnival.
The carnival gathered various exhibitors and local entrepreneurs offering goods, food, beverages and essential items for Deepavali. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak’s education opportunities are for all races, says PBB vice-president
Article:
SIBU, Nov 7 — Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Vice President Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee has defended the Sarawak government’s inclusive policy of providing educational opportunities to all races, while reminding the Bumiputera community not to be left behind in seizing the opportunities provided.
He said the Bumiputera community should not question the opportunities given to other races, but should instead ensure that their children take advantage of the state government’s educational and development opportunities.
“What we need to worry about is not the opportunities opened to others. What we should worry about is whether our Bumiputera children are seizing those open opportunities.
“Do not worry at all that other communities are given opportunities because in Sarawak, every layer of society will be given opportunities as long as they have the appropriate qualifications,” he said when speaking at the Nangka Youth Friendly Dinner here last night.
The incumbent Nangka state assemblyman said that throughout his 15 years representing the area, he has adhered to the principle that no community should be sidelined from development regardless of their racial background.
Meanwhile, Dr Annuar acknowledged that not all public issues could be resolved throughout his tenure, but stressed that every trust given will continue to be carried out to the best of his ability. — Bernama

Title: Hassan Karim urges Melaka voters to judge Pakatan on federal government track record
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 7 — Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) track record as a key component of the federal government should serve as a yardstick for Melaka voters to assess the coalition’s capabilities ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14, said Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim.
He said the government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had a good record in governance, particularly in creating employment opportunities for the people.
“Official government employment and investment statistics show that hundreds of thousands of new jobs have been and are being generated by the Madani government,” he said in an open message to Melaka voters and the public yesterday.
Citing data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Hassan said the domestic economy had generated an average of 20,000 to 35,000 new jobs every quarter between 2023 and 2026, in line with a decline in the unemployment rate to between 3.1 and 3.3 per cent.
He said the RM329.5 billion in approved investments in 2023 were expected to generate more than 127,000 new jobs, including over 36,500 in the digital and technology sectors.
“For 2024 and 2025, approved investments contributed to the creation of between 120,000 and 140,000 new job opportunities across the manufacturing and services sectors,” he said, citing the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA).
Hassan said the government was targeting at least 30,000 new high-skilled and technology-based jobs for local youths and graduates.
He said the government also aimed to create tens of thousands of new medium- and high-income jobs by 2027 through initiatives involving HRD Corp, the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
Hassan also highlighted foreign investors’ confidence in the national economy, citing Google’s announcement of a US$15 billion (about RM61.1 billion) investment in Malaysia, which is expected to create 37,000 jobs by 2027.
“These are not political propaganda. These are facts that the people of Melaka and Malaysia can assess for themselves as the results of the work of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Madani government in creating jobs for Malaysians,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10. — Bernama

Title: Selangor Sultan marks 25-year reign with foundation to support education, community welfare
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah last night graced the official launch of Yayasan Sultan Selangor at a Royal Charity Gala Dinner held in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebrations of his reign.
Also present was the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, accompanied by the Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Datuk Abdul Aziz.
Upon arrival, their Royal Highnesses toured a special exhibition, which featured a retrospective display highlighting Sultan Sharafuddin’s 25-year reign.
In his royal address, Tengku Amir Shah, who chaired the Royal Charity Gala Dinner, said the foundation was a meaningful gift to commemorate his father’s Silver Jubilee, with the aim of creating a lasting impact for generations to come.
“Twenty-five years on the throne is more than a milestone. It is a quarter of a century of service, guidance, and unwavering care for the people of Selangor.
“It is fitting that we mark it not with celebration alone, but with a gift, that will keep giving for generations to come,” he said.
Tengku Amir Shah said Yayasan Sultan Selangor stands on four pillars namely community welfare, education and scholarships, heritage and cultural preservation, as well as emergency assistance.
He said the
yayasan
would work closely with Yayasan Raja Muda Selangor and Selangor Youth Community to create opportunities, nurture young people and support the welfare of the community.
On the foundation’s education initiative, Tengku Amir Shah said its first Sultan of Selangor Scholar, Atiqah Nor Azlan, began her Master’s in Public Policy at the, University of Oxford, in September.
He expressed hope that many more deserving young Malaysians would benefit from the foundation’s support to study at leading institutions worldwide.
Part of the funds raised at the gala dinner would also be channelled to charitable organisations that had maintained close ties with Sultan Sharafuddin and the Selangor royal family over the past 25 years, he added.
The event also featured a special documentary titled “25 Years – One Enduring Bond”, produced by Bernama TV Creative Video Unit, highlighting key milestones of the Sultan’s 25-year reign. — Bernama

Title: Unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses face closure, demolition under Selangor crackdown
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Selangor State Executive Council has directed all local authorities in the state to take immediate enforcement action against unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses.
State Islamic Religious Affairs and Innovation Committee chairman Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the action would target premises operating without licences from local authorities and those without certified slaughterers.
“Enforcement action must be carried out in accordance with existing laws to ensure that these premises are closed and, where appropriate, demolished.
“This is to prevent non-halal chicken from entering the state’s supply chain, an issue that has raised concerns among Muslims in Selangor,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Mohammad Fahmi also advised the public, particularly Muslims, to purchase raw or cooked chicken only from premises with valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) issued by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
He said the public could check the list of halal-certified premises through the Halal Malaysia Portal at
www.halal.gov.my
and report any suspected unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses to the local authorities or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais).
“The Selangor government remains committed to ensuring a steady supply of halal chicken at affordable prices for the people of the state,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Singapore-based Bitdeer eyes further investment in Malaysia’s AI infrastructure, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Singapore-headquartered Bitdeer Technologies Group (Bitdeer) has expressed its intention to continue investing in Malaysia due to its confidence in the Madani government’s direction and policies on digital transformation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was conveyed to him during a courtesy visit from Bitdeer founder, chairman and chief executive officer Jihan Wu, along with his delegation, earlier yesterday.
The Nasdaq-listed company, which provides cloud computing services for artificial intelligence (AI) and Bitcoin mining infrastructure, is currently finetuning a long-term investment proposal to develop world-class AI infrastructure in Malaysia, Anwar said in a post on X.
“I emphasised that such an investment must create job opportunities and provide training to develop the expertise of Malaysians, particularly in AI, engineering and advanced computing.
“The Madani government will continue to facilitate strategic investments such as this to ensure that the growth of the digital economy also strengthens local industries and creates more high-value job opportunities for Malaysians,” Anwar added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia must speed up agricultural modernisation to strengthen food security, says Mat Sabu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Malaysia must accelerate the modernisation of its agricultural sector and improve production efficiency to strengthen food security amid growing challenges, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said Malaysia could learn from countries such as Brazil, which had significantly increased its agricultural output, particularly corn, through a market guarantee system rather than relying solely on subsidies.
Recounting his meeting with his Brazilian counterpart, Mohamad said Brazil’s approach did not involve providing subsidies to farmers. Instead, the government guaranteed to purchase produce that could not be sold in the market.
“Regardless of how much they produce, the government guarantees to buy any unsold produce. This motivates farmers to work harder and increase their output, knowing that the government will purchase what they cannot sell,” he said.
He was speaking at the Malaysia Madani Intellectual Forum Series 14 here last night, moderated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir, SD Guthrie Berhad Group President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute CEO Sarena Che Omar.
On the RM2.6 billion in subsidies allocated for local paddy production, Mohamad said calls to discontinue the subsidies and rely solely on government purchases of rice were not appropriate.
He said paddy farmers still needed continued support and encouragement to improve production.
“There has been progress, but we are moving a little slowly. At Mada (Muda Agricultural Development Authority), yields of eight to nine tonnes can already be achieved, although not by many farmers. We need to accelerate the shift towards modernisation,” he said.
On other food commodities, Malaysia had achieved self-sufficiency in fish through the rapid growth of its aquaculture sector, he said, adding that domestic chicken and egg production was also sufficient to meet the country’s needs.
To reduce dependence on imports, the ministry was promoting grain corn cultivation in collaboration with major companies, with a target of meeting 30 per cent of domestic demand by 2030.
The ministry was also expanding onion cultivation based on research by the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi), he said.
Mohamad also stressed the need to strengthen links between agricultural research institutions and universities and farmers, citing Thailand as an example.
“If we visit an agricultural university in Thailand and spend two or three hours there, we can see groups of farmers coming in and out. We need to strengthen this link so that technology developed today can reach rural communities by tomorrow,” he said.
On geopolitical security and future threats, Mohamad urged the public to be prepared for possible cyberwarfare that could disrupt food supply chains, as some European countries were already experiencing supply disruptions and food inflation.
However, he assured that the country’s basic food supplies were sufficient, with rice buffer stocks available for at least six months and fish supplies for eight months.
The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) was also prepared to manage physical food distribution should access to digital systems be disrupted, he said.
On weather-related challenges, Mohamad said the ministry was monitoring forecasts by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) on the El Nino phenomenon, which could bring extreme temperatures of up to 40°C after December.
He advised padi farmers to follow the stipulated planting schedules to ensure prudent management of water resources at the three main dams in the Mada area.
“If water levels at the dams become critically low, we will reduce water supply to padi fields and prioritise domestic needs. We take into account the views of scientists, meteorologists and universities to ensure food security is maintained,” he said. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia eyes stronger defence ties with Turkiye, with focus on technology transfer
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia views its defence cooperation with Turkiye as a strategic avenue to strengthen its technological capabilities, deepen bilateral relations and contribute to regional stability in South-east Asia.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the partnership extends beyond the procurement of defence equipment to include knowledge and technology transfer, while opening up opportunities for broader cooperation in economic, technological, educational and diplomatic fields.
He said military diplomacy was equally important in ensuring South-east Asia remained peaceful and politically stable, particularly amid growing competition and influence from major powers.
“Military diplomacy is also important because we would like to see South-east Asia remain a peaceful region. We have to maintain political stability in Asean as a whole, as we must try to prevent superpowers from exerting influence over Asean member countries,” he said during a session titled “Turkiye From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor” at the TRT World Forum 2026 here yesterday.
The session also featured the Director of Foreign Policy Studies at the Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (SETA), Prof Murat Yesiltas; Atlantic Council Nonresident Senior Fellow Rich Outzen; American Arab Centre President Farah Al-Atassi; and United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the rural and regional development minister, expressed strong confidence that deepened defence and technological cooperation will propel both nations toward realising their ambitious US$10 billion bilateral trade target, while creating a more balanced and vibrant trade relationship.
“From the perspective of both countries, the target is achievable, especially with Malaysia’s procurement of defence and security equipment. We have already received the Littoral Mission Ship (LMS) as well as unmanned aerial vehicles,” he added.
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Turkiye currently stands at US$5.6 billion, with both countries agreeing in Jan 2026 to raise the figure to US$10 billion within the next five years.
The target reflects their shared commitment to expanding economic ties, with Malaysia among Turkiye’s key trading partners in South-east Asia, alongside Singapore.
Malaysia and Turkiye established formal diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close cooperation across various sectors, including politics, trade, economy and education.
The TRT World Forum 2026, themed “A World Without a Centre: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?”, brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives from around the world to exchange views on pressing global issues.
Among the prominent Malaysians who have participated in the forum over the years are Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 and 2019, former international trade and industry minister Tan Sri Rafidah Aziz (2019) and public health expert Prof Tan Sri Jemilah Mahmood (2020). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Turkiye set US$10b trade target by 2030 following Zahid-Erdogan discussions
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkiye President Recep Tayyip Erdogan here on Friday, with discussions focusing on strengthening bilateral relations and increasing Malaysia-Turkiye trade value.
The 30-minute meeting, starting at 4pm local time (9pm Malaysian time), occurred shortly after Erdogan launched the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC), before Ahmad Zahid joined a session titled “Turkiye From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor”.
During the meeting, both countries agreed to increase their bilateral trade target from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030, following the establishment of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council (HLSCC), which held its inaugural meeting in Ankara last January.
Ahmad Zahid also touched on Turkiye’s role as the 12th Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner and Malaysia’s commitment as the coordinating country for Asean-Turkiye relations to expand strategic cooperation between both parties.
He also expressed appreciation for Turkiye’s firm commitment to championing regional peace, including its active involvement in Syria, Lebanon and Palestine, alongside its role as a mediator in the Russia-Ukraine conflict through the “Istanbul Process”.
Discussions also covered developments in diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between the United States and Iran, including joint initiatives mobilised by Turkiye alongside Pakistan, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.
Furthermore, Ahmad Zahid conveyed Malaysia’s strong support for Turkiye’s role in hosting the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled to take place in Antalya on November 11 and 12.
Earlier, Ahmad Zahid received a courtesy call from Turkiye’s Council of Higher Education (YOK) President Prof Erol Ozvar at the hotel where he is staying here, besides holding a bilateral meeting with Turkiye Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz at the ICC.
The deputy prime minister is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from November 5 to 8 in conjunction with his participation in the TRT World Forum 2026.
The two-day forum, themed “A World Without a Centre: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?”, gathers political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives globally. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia rises two spots in good governance ranking, Anwar warns against complacency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Malaysia’s rise to 40th place among 133 countries in the Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) 2026 recognises the government’s continuous efforts to strengthen national administrative capacity, integrity and effectiveness, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“This achievement is no excuse for us to be complacent. There is still room for attention, specifically in strengthening inter-agency coordination and ensuring every policy and plan is executed more efficiently and effectively,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
He said the Madani government’s priority remains building robust institutions, improving public service delivery and ensuring every development effort brings tangible benefits to the people.
“Ultimately, a government’s success is not merely measured through its ranking in international indices, but through changes that can be felt in the people’s lives,” he added.
Malaysia climbed two spots from 42nd in 2025 in the index, which evaluates national governance performance across seven core pillars.
The seven pillars are Leadership and Foresight, Attractive Marketplace, Financial Stewardship, Robust Laws and Policies, Global Influence and Reputation, Helping People Rise, and Strong Institutions.
In the 2026 list, Malaysia ranks behind China in 39th place, Slovakia (38th) and Saudi Arabia (37th).
Singapore maintained its top position for the fourth consecutive year since 2023, followed by Norway in second place and Denmark in third. — Bernama

Title: Selangor freezes Puncak Alam development works, orders faster flood mitigation measures
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Selangor State Executive Council has decided to immediately halt all development works in Puncak Alam, Kuala Selangor, while flood mitigation plans and the Environmental Impact Assessment are reassessed.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said at the same time, the Public Works Department will temporarily close Jalan Batu Arang in Rawang following a collapsed bank to facilitate repair works.
“Additionally, small and large scale flood mitigation works statewide, especially in higher-risk areas, must be expedited immediately rather than following conventional schedules, as rain is expected almost daily.
“We are facing a climate change crisis and the flood mitigation work culture must match the current challenges to prevent any harm to the people,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Amirudin said the state government acknowledges that the rain causing floods in several areas has inconvenienced the people, particularly those commuting to work and fetching children from school, bringing anxiety whenever it rains.
Therefore, public criticism directed at any government agency must be accepted openly with a commitment to redouble efforts to help affected flood victims and prevent daily recurrences.
“The people cannot afford to hear excuses from any agency if floods occur; instead, they want to live safely without worrying about their personal safety or their loved ones,” he said.
Furthermore, Amirudin said the state government will expedite and increase aid for flood victims at temporary evacuation centres (PPS), while accelerating house repairs and cleaning via state agencies and Yayasan MBI.
Aid of up to RM1,500 from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the state government will be channelled to victims at PPS to ease their current financial burden while repair works proceed.
“Early warnings will also be given to road users in areas at risk of rising water levels on roads, while the Drainage and Irrigation Department implements immediate water diversion works.
“All agencies have been given a collective responsibility to ensure drain and river maintenance works are carried out faster and immediately without any delay,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s Taman Duta residence gazetted as prison, house arrest deferred pending legal clarification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The residence of former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak on Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, has been declared a prison for the imprisonment or detention of persons in lawful custody.
The declaration was made by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995 [Act 537].
The official document is set out in the Federal Government Gazette dated yesterday and published on the official portal of the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC).
According to the gazette, the declared area covers all buildings and a land area of 4,558.975 square metres at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, situated on Lot 5746, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, District of Kuala Lumpur.
“In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995 [Act 537], the Minister declares all buildings and the area measuring 4,558.975 square metres at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, 50480 Kuala Lumpur, situated on Lot 5746, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, District of Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, to be a prison for the purposes of the Act for the imprisonment or detention of persons in lawful custody,” the gazette stated.
The declaration takes effect on the date it was sealed, which is yesterday.
Najib has reportedly settled the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International Sdn Bhd fund misappropriation case at the Criminal Registry of the High Court here yesterday.
The payment is one of the conditions of the conditional pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on September 18, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
However, in a statement yesterday evening, the AGC said the implementation of house arrest for the former Prime Minister should be temporarily deferred pending further scrutiny and clarification of the interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order and the effect of the Order of Discharge.
The AGC added that throughout the deferment period, Najib should remain at his current place of detention, subject to the powers and directions of the relevant authorities. — Bernama

Title: Anwar open to easing foreign worker rules for sectors facing shortages, warns against exploitation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is prepared to consider easing foreign worker approval requirements for sectors facing genuine manpower shortages, particularly the plantation sector.
Speaking at the 14th Forum Ilmuwan Malaysia Madani in Kuala Lumpur last night, Anwar said the proposal followed requests from industry players struggling to recruit workers for specific tasks, such as harvesting oil palm fruit.
He said approvals could be considered for such tasks, provided employers committed to reducing their reliance on foreign labour through mechanisation.
Anwar also said he had instructed the relevant authorities to simplify approval procedures for certain urgent labour needs.
“Plantations are asking for workers. I agree if they are specifically for harvesting, but many plantations also use them for other purposes.
“So, while I agree with the request, I think I will take this up with the relevant ministers.
“If the workers are specifically needed for harvesting, we can approve the request, provided they give an undertaking that they will reduce their dependence on foreign labour through mechanisation,” Anwar said.
He suggested reviewing how foreign workers are deployed within large plantations, including shifting manpower from adequately staffed activities to those facing shortages, which he described as a fairer arrangement.
Anwar also questioned why some plantations, despite substantial profits, had yet to invest meaningfully in automation and mechanisation to reduce their reliance on foreign labour.
He went on to criticise major companies for resisting wage increases despite substantial profits, citing one company that had made RM1 billion but was unwilling to raise monthly pay by just RM20.
Beyond labour shortages, Anwar raised concerns about the treatment of foreign workers, condemning exploitative practices by some employers.
“We bring in foreign workers, but sometimes the treatment is so dehumanising.
“We talk about Madani, social justice and so on, yet look at how some factories house their workers in conditions resembling those of slaves a hundred years ago.
“I cannot accept that,” he said.
Anwar also raised concerns over recruitment syndicates and excessive fees, saying the government was negotiating with individual source countries to reduce costs and protect workers from exploitation.
He stressed that recruitment fees must be reasonable and should not impose an undue financial burden on workers, particularly given the inflated charges imposed by some agents.
“Previously, agents would take workers’ wages and keep their passports. I describe this as modern slavery, and we cannot condone it.
“Although I agree, and I have taken important note of the concerns raised tonight about reviewing certain aspects of foreign worker requirements, including those for specific plantation activities, we must remember that there must be firm action against any form of abuse, including the exploitation of foreign workers.
“They are not our slaves, and excessive actions taken against foreigners are also unjustified,” he said.
The forum, which focused on national resilience in food security amid global uncertainties, was moderated by Anwar and attended by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, SD Guthrie Berhad Group President and CEO Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute CEO Sarena Che Omar.

Title: Deepavali or Diwali? The story behind the two names of the Festival of Lights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — As Malaysians prepare to celebrate Deepavali tomorrow, a linguistic debate about the Festival of Lights still lingers: is it Deepavali or Diwali?
Though it may come as a surprise to many, there is only one proper term for the festival — and it is actually Deepavali for both the North and South Indian traditions.
Malay Mail
explains how the name came about and what the festival truly entails:
What does Deepavali celebrate?
Deepavali is traditionally observed on Naraka Chaturdasi, the fourteenth lunar day of the waning moon in the Aippasi month of the Tamil calendar, according to Malaysia Hindu Sangam president Genesan Thangavellu.
Genesan said Deepavali marks the triumph of Lord Krishna and his consort Satyabhama over the demon Narakasura, symbolising the victory of righteousness over evil and the removal of ignorance.
In North Indian traditions, Deepavali also marks the homecoming of Lord Rama and his queen Sita to Ayodhya after defeating the demon Ravana and completing their 14-year exile.
Goddess Lakshmi is also worshipped on this day to seek wealth and prosperity.
New Year for Gujaratis
Interestingly, Deepavali also marks the end of the Gujarati calendar, with the community celebrating the Gujarati New Year, or Bestu Varas, the very next day, according to Shree Lakshmi Narayan Mandir president Rajesh Kamani.
Rajesh said the celebrations begin two days before Deepavali with a prayer to Goddess Lakshmi on Dhanteras, when devotees also purchase gold or silver to welcome growth and prosperity into their households.
On New Year morning, Gujaratis also buy salt to welcome good luck, as salt is called
sabras
in the Gujarati language, which means “all things good”.
Those running businesses also worship their new account books along with Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha in a ceremony called Chopda Pujan.
“We write
shubh labh
(or auspicious gains in Gujarati) and draw a
swastik
on the first page, which basically opens the new financial year,” Rajesh explained.
Why are there two names for the same festival?
A Happy Diwali decoration is displayed at a stall selling festive decorations and snacks ahead of Deepavali celebrations, October 22, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
The term Deepavali is more prominent in South Indian traditions, while Diwali is more synonymous with North Indian ethnic groups.
However, Shree Lakshmi Narayan Mandir vice-president Anil Sharma said Deepavali is the most apt term as the festival derives its name from the Sanskrit word Dipavali.
In Sanskrit, Dipavali means a row of lights, as
dipa
refers to a lamp, while
avali
means a row or line.
“The proper term is still Deepavali although it has been abbreviated into Diwali mainly in the north,” Anil said.
Similarly, Genesan said using Deepavali would be more appropriate since the term is formally recognised in the First Schedule of the Holidays Act 1951.
How do celebrations differ between South and North India?
Although both names refer to the Festival of Lights, the duration and customs of celebrations can differ by region and community.
In parts of South India, Deepavali is observed mainly over one day, and Anil said the day begins early in the morning with a traditional oil bath, known as
ennai kuliyal
or
ganga snanam
.
This is followed by prayers, donning new clothes and seeking blessings from elders.
“Families prepare traditional sweets and savouries, decorate their homes with
kolam
, light oil lamps and visit temples to offer prayers,” he said.
Meanwhile, Deepavali celebrations span five days in North Indian traditions, according to Anil.
The first day, Dhanteras, is associated with worship and the purchase of items such as gold, silver or new utensils by some families as symbols of prosperity and good fortune.
On the second day, Naraka Chaturdashi, also known as Choti Diwali, Hindus in the north perform the Kali Chaudas prayer to Goddess Kali to dispel fear, suffering and negative energy.
The main Deepavali day is marked by prayers to Goddess Lakshmi, who is associated with wealth and prosperity, and the lighting of lamps.
Anil said Deepavali also commemorates the homecoming of Lord Rama and Goddess Sita to Ayodhya.
The fourth day is associated with Govardhan Puja, which recalls the story of Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill to protect villagers from torrential rain.
According to Rajesh, temples prepare the
annakut
, literally a mountain of food comprising dozens of dishes, to be offered to Lord Krishna on this day.
Deepavali celebrations in the north culminate with Bhai Dooj or Bhai Tikka on the fifth day, celebrating the enduring bonds between siblings through the story of Lord Yama and his sister Yamuna.
“On this day, sisters apply a ceremonial
tikka
(made from red vermilion powder) on their brothers’ foreheads and pray for their happiness, health and longevity.
“The brothers provide gifts and promise lifelong care for their sisters,” Anil explained.
So, while Happy Diwali is still an acceptable greeting for the Festival of Lights, Happy Deepavali remains the more apt term across the board.

Title: If Malaysia plans to roll out a new long-term care insurance, what lessons can be learned from Singapore?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — If Malaysia was to introduce its own national insurance for long-term care (especially for older persons), could the Singapore experience be a useful reference?
Here’s a quick look at the Singapore government’s national long-term care insurance CareShield Life, provided via its equivalent to Malaysia’s Employees Provident Fund which is the Central Provident Fund (CPF).
In 2020, Singapore launched CareShield Life which offers lifelong monthly cash payouts if one becomes severely disabled and needs long-term care.
According to Singapore’s Health Ministry, severe disability may be due to sudden events such as strokes and spinal cord injuries; or worsening chronic diseases such as diabetes; or illnesses in old age such as dementia.
CareShield Life automatically enrols and covers all Singapore citizens and permanent residents when they turn 30, and they cannot opt out as it is a mandatory scheme.
Here’s how it works, based on information from Singapore’s CPF:
1. Paying the premium until age 67 (unless severely disabled earlier), getting coverage for life
The premiums are paid once a year and automatically deducted from Singaporeans’ MediSave account in CPF.
(In CPF, workers’ savings go to three accounts for three main purposes — retirement, housing, and healthcare. MediSave is for healthcare.)
You will pay the premiums from 30 until 67 (generally working years for Singaporeans), which means lower annual premiums as you are spreading out the premium payments over a longer period.
The premiums paid by CPF members in each age group will be used for the expected future payouts to the same cohort, which helps ensure the insurance stays sustainable.
As CareShield Life payouts increase annually to keep up with rising long-term care costs, the premiums also increase annually (based on actuarial reviews and factors such as changes in life expectancy and disability trends).
If you are receiving payouts, you will stop paying premiums (even though you are not yet 67) and will only resume paying premiums if you no longer have a severe disability.
2. Government subsidies to keep it affordable
Unlike private insurance that stops coverage if you stop paying premiums, the Singapore government provides financial support to ensure no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to financial difficulties:
The government subsidises up to 30 per cent of the premiums for lower-income and middle-income Singaporeans (depending on their household per capita income, and if they only own one property, and the annual value of their residence is not more than S$31,000 or RM98,280).
For those who still cannot afford to pay premiums even after subsidies, the government will provide Additional Premium Support.
3. Getting assessed to see if you are severely disabled
You can get payouts if an assessment shows you are severely disabled:
Which means you cannot carry out at least three of these six activities of daily living (feeding, dressing, washing yourself, toileting, walking or moving around, transferring from a bed to a chair or vice versa).
A person with dementia or cognitive impairment will not automatically qualify for payouts and will still need to be assessed, as the impact of dementia on their functional abilities may differ.
A severe disability assessor who is accredited by Singapore’s Health Ministry (doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists or nurses) will do the assessment.
The first assessment is free.
You have to pay for subsequent assessments (S$100 at a clinic, S$250 at your home) from your own pocket, and will be reimbursed only if you are assessed to have severe disability.
Alternatively, someone who is already receiving care at a nursing home can get a free assessment and submit a Resident Assessment Form, without needing to go through a separate disability assessment.
4. Monthly payouts for life (if still severely disabled)
As people may have different long-term care needs and preferences (e.g. getting care while staying at home, or moving into a nursing home), CareShield Life pays out cash so you can have more flexibility in choosing and deciding on your care.
You can also arrange for the payouts to be paid directly to your nursing home.
The monthly payout amount is currently S$689 in 2026, and the potential amount you can get will continue increasing every year until you turn 67 or once you make a successful claim.
In other words, you will get a higher monthly payout if you claim at a later age, and the payout amount will be fixed once you start receiving them.
For example, someone aged 30 will receive $689 per month for life if they claim for severe disability in 2026, but will receive an estimated $2,941 per month for life if they only develop severe disability and claim at age 67.
A long-term care insurance for just the basics
CareShield Life is a non-profit government-managed insurance that is only intended as basic financial support for long-term care needs for those who are severely disabled.
It is aimed at complementing other government subsidies and assistance, personal savings, support from family and the community; with government safety nets available for those who cannot afford long-term care.
Those who want more insurance benefits can top up by buying supplements from private insurance companies.
CareShield Life does not cover those with mild or moderate disabilities in order to keep the premiums affordable, while those with such conditions can use existing Singapore government subsidies and grants for their long-term care.
Socso deputy CEO (Strategy and Corporate) Edmund Cheong said a mandatory long-term care insurance is needed as personal savings would be insufficient to pay for such care, and that it would benefit all Malaysians as they would all eventually grow old. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
What do we have in Malaysia now?
Currently, the Social Security Organisation (Socso) provides something similar to long-term care protection under its
Invalidity Scheme
, but only if the Socso contributor is certified to be invalid before age 60.
Under the Invalidity Scheme, Socso pays a monthly payout called the Invalidity Pension as long as the contributor remains invalid or until their death, with the amount at 50 to 65 per cent of the average assumed monthly wage. The payout is at a minimum RM550 per month.
After the contributor dies, their dependents such as their spouse or children will receive a monthly Survivors’ Pension.
The Invalidity Scheme also pays a fixed monthly allowance of RM500 if a person is certified to need constant personal care from another person, and pays for physiotherapy and rehabilitation and medical aids such as wheelchair and crutches.
During the recent National Long-Term Care Financing Dialogue 2026, Socso deputy CEO (Strategy and Corporate) Edmund Cheong Peck Huang proposed that Malaysia introduce a national long-term care insurance that would feature mandatory affordable contributions and cover all Malaysians, even beyond 60.
The government’s 13th Malaysia Plan states that a long-term care (LTC) insurance scheme “will be explored to provide a structured and sustainable protection”.
It remains to be seen if the government would introduce a national LTC insurance, and if it could be built on existing platforms such as Socso or EPF, or if any elements might be adopted from other countries’ models.
